title: It has been a year sense taking delivery.
text:
It has been just over a year since getting my Timberline 850 delivered and I am just as excited about using it today as I was then!  

The quality of the unit is solid, it looks just as good today as the day I purchased it and working great.  The D2 controller is awesome, super easy to use and the temps are maintained to within few degrees (I have tested with other thermometers).  Some have stated problems with connecting to WiFi but I had no trouble at all, first time it worked seamlessly.  I love the D2 and Wifi, I have controlled the temps of my grill from across town and getting the alerts on the probe temps has allowed me to switch to the keep warm mode within the App which has been awesome.

  I live in Ottawa, Canada and I have used my Timberline on the coldest of days (-40) with no problems at all, shovel a path to it and it has always started up and heated up with no problems at all.  It does have a cold weather start setting so it takes a few minutes longer to start.  The all around double wall construction is what made me pick the Timberline due to the cold temps and I am glad I did.  I also keep mine very clean and vacuum out the dust regularly and wipe down the inside and outside of the grill often, looks brand new still.  

Everything I cook on the grill has been exceptional, especially any type of poultry from full roast turkeys to chicken breasts or thighs, always juicy and flavourful.  I have done Prime Ribs roasts, reverse seared and the taste was superb with the right about of smoke.  Ribs have always been great and the queso dip with chorizo sausage is always a hit with guests.   

I also purchased the rib rack recently and love that I can fit a ton of ribs on it and it fits the grill nicely. I also like the orange tray I ordered with it, nice for pulling meats off and for serving outside too.

After a year+ I am very happy with the purchase and by the looks of things, this thing will last many many years as well.  Only downfall, the cover for it has began to fade and show a lot of aging, a bit of leaking too, that is disappointing.    

I would highly recommend the Timberline 850, I have been happy with the performance, size and most of all the cook results, everything is always delicious.

title: Want to be Traeger Dedicated- But Let Down
text:
We loved the Traeger when we first got it. Traegered everything from meat, to bread, cookies, sides- you name it, but within 3 months it began having issues with pellets getting stuck in the auger. Replaced auger motor in the first six months. My husband had to clean out the auger 5-6 times in the last year. Often has issues with the temperature dropping and shuts itself off OR temperature keeps rising and has burnt pellets in the auger. 

Today was the last straw (for me)- after taking the a Traeger Shop Class which was great- we were smoking a $100+ brisket and the tempertature dropped and then temperature shot up. Had to stop the smoke and finish in the oven :(

For an almost $1000 grill we are pretty disappointed and would not recommend the pro-series. Smokes great- when it works- not dependable.

title: Incredibly easy from start to cleanup!
text: I’ve had a hardwood charcoal smoker for years, and enjoyed it, but getting the fire going was tedious, and cleanup a greasy pain. Bought this Traeger as a gift to myself. Didn’t really know what to expect. It has exceeded my wildest expectations! Super easy to get going, cleanup is next to nothing, the different combinations of wood pellets are wonderful and incredibly aromatic, the end product... ribs, pork loins, briskets, whatever... out-freaking-standing! Can’t say enough good things about this product!

title: Traded Up but Wish I Hadn’t
text:
Got rid of my pro for a Timberline 850. Wish I’d kept the Pro. Had to replace thermocouple as it kept running away. Temp got so hot that it bubbled the paint and 6 months later I’m still waiting for part. 

Wi-Fi is un reliable and keeps dropping out. You can troubleshoot and troubleshoot connects then drops out. 

Save your money buy the pro.

title: If there was six stars I’d rate it seven
text: Got the grill last Xmas and by far the greatest gift of all time, it didn’t take long to master this baby. And now when I turn the switch on people start gathering brisket is my favorite, melt in your mouth and simple all you need is a grill from Traeger and time and rest comes natural like wood pellets

title: Great Purchase!
text: I have been very happy with this grill overall.  The only annoying thing was with the WiFire technology on initial setup.  They tell you it needs to be within 15 feet of your router.  Mine is probably 30 feet away.  I needed to connect a WiFi extender to make the WiFire work. Luckily I already had one from my last house. I would think you would just include an extender in the purchase if the range is so short.  Anyway, I was able to connect and I love the grill, the app, and the food that comes off of the grill.  Super addition to our life!!

title: good smoke
text: Hello I have a Pro 34  and the auger weld snapped off from the stainless steel rod attached to the motor and a LEr error happened. This grill is still new, used 5-6 times.Due to work this grill sat in the box new for some time and I am sure the warranty is expired. I will not drop any more money into this grill.I think I will look into getting a higher end grill . The pro 34 must be a budget style.

title: Everything it's cracked up to be and more!
text: I bought my Ironwood 885 6 months ago, I cook on it every weekend and more from boston butt and ribs to fresh caught redfish and beer can chicken. My wife has even fired it up on her own while I'v been at work and baked deserts and made smoked chili.

title: Traeger the VERY BEST
text: I have had TRAGER'S since the late '90s, the one I bought this year to replace the second one is the IRONWOOD 560' during the spring to late fall I use mine twice to three times a day, baking, grilling, smoking, (nice to cook outside to keep the heat out) the other two were great units I just totally wore them out, each one has had great new improvements.

title: Horrible business practice
text: I purchased a grill and was told it would be here before Thanksgiving and when I called to ask why i was only getting accessories, I was than told they were on backorder for almost a month. If they had told me that upfront and had been honest I would have just went to the local ACE and bought one there. I know I don't mean a hill of beans in the grand scheme of their company but service and reputation are everything in business. I guess they are too big for us little people now.

title: Idiot proof
text: My wife bought me the Timberland 570 via QVC.  I give her a lot of trouble about buying stuff on QVC but not this time.  It is basically the Pro 575.  The smoker is idiot proof.  Follow the recipe and cook like a pro.  I have had some difficulty in getting the smoker to fire up between cooking but have found that if I clean the "heat pan" before firing up this issue is eliminated.

title: Disappointed in product performance post assembly
text:
I bought this product yesterday based on recommendations for grills from people i know and trust because they have plenty of grilling / smoking experience.  I was excited to get the product home from Home Depot and assembled so i could try it out before the holidays.  Setup was straight forward and easy enough.
Once i had everything put together, it was time to fire it up, which means priming the auger and then heating the grill. Unfortunately, the auger wouldn't push pellets into the burn chamber and would repeatedly get stuck.  I tried to free the auger with the capability included, but to no avail.  My wife and I have each called to try to work through this, and were given options of exchanging the product at Home Depot, removing and replacing the auger mechanism and now, we will be replacing the auger mechanism ourselves based on the latest call with support staff.  
I know others have had difficulty with auger performance, but I didnt expect that for the very first use of the product.  It is really surprising to experience this with an $800 product that is so highly regarded.  I can only hope that i will have success as a BBQ repair man and then experience all of the same joy that others have written about.  Until then, I will look out my back window at a nice looking grill that is a step backwards from the propane grill that i moved to my shed.

title: flimsy
text: i have had my grill for 5 years it is a piece of junk you have to check it every 30 min. to see if it's still running it just stops smoking

title: PRO 575 - SUPER EASY TO USE
text: THE PRO 575 WORKS PERFECTLY EVERY TIME.  HOLDS TEMPS LIKE A CHARM AND FOOD COOKS EVENLY.  GREAT PELLET GRILL.  MY ONLY DOWNSIDE TO THE PRO COMPARED TO THE BRONSON, (which I also have), THE PRO 575 DOES NOT PRODUCE A LOT OF SMOKE AND THUS FOOD DOES NOT HAVE THE HEAVY SMOKE FLAVOR.

title: Solid temperature control
text: I just bought the timberline 1300 and used it for the Thanksgiving turkey. The temperature control is frighteningly good- set to 325, it brought the temperature up to about 335, settled at 324-326 for the rest of the cook. I have retired a Traeger Texas Elite 34 which varied 30+ degrees on both sides of the set temperature despite replacing the controller three times, the fans twice, etc., etc. I put up with it because the meat tasted so good... until it started just turning off in the middle of the cook. I bought the pre-assembled 1300 at ACE hardware. No trouble with the wire-fire set up even though I later found that ACE had not connected the antenna. It works even better now. My turkey was superb. If it continues to function this well for the coming years, I'll become a Traeger evangelist!

title: Terrible
text: Worst grill to ever buy don’t buy this grill save your money for a real grill that doesn’t really on poor parts and electricity.

title: Great Grill - Impressive & Rare Customer Service
text:
I bought the first generation of this grill (Ironwood) and loved it except for one thing: the grease system did not work correctly and the grill frequently caught fire, because of that. After working with customer service many times but unable to fix the problem, Traeger replaced my grill with a new one.  Jessica, the service rep was extremely helpful and though I am sure Traeger lost money on my grill, I will remain a Traeger customer and continue to recommend this grill. It works and looks great!

This type of customer service and support of a product is extremely rare these days.

title: Awesome Grill
text: I bought my Pro 22 for myself as a early birthday gift, I seasoned it and my first grilling was 2 whole chickens a rack of ribs and some pork spare ribs and a pork roast and all turned out amazing! Then the following weekend a brisket!

title: Do NOT waste your money!
text: Wish I would’ve bought a Pit Boss smoker from Lowe’s. I’ve had this grill for less than a month and I’ve been through two door seals. Every time you open the door it snags and gets snatched out. It’s chipped the “durable” coating on the grill. Which of it was of any quality it should NOT have chipped from the same material (and thickness) of a paper clip. Also, the hopper does not feed the pellets properly. It will read empty, and when I go out and check it’s still 60% full. So, I have to stick my fingers between the grates and try and move them around. A $2000 dollar grill should not be doing this. Should’ve bought the cheapest one they had. As I bought this one for the “insulation” (lack there of at this point). I just want my money back, but good luck with that, haha.

title: Know What It Is
text: After years of harassment from my daughter, I finally gave in and picked up an Ironwood 650 during a Black Friday Sale. I chose to take a boxed one so it would be easier to transport home. Assembly was a breeze, though I would caution folks to make sure they remove the protective cover from the temperature probe. The directions made no mention of this step and I only discovered the error during the seasoning process when the  indicated temperature continued to climb well past what I had it set at. Fortunately I caught it in time and removed the melted plastic before any damage occured and continued the seasoning process. That evening I attempted my first product, a grilled Delmonico Steak. As warned by a friend, grilling steaks is not this grill's strong point. Undeterred, I tried again the next day with smoked burgers. They took much longer than my gas grill and what the recipe stated, but the results were exceptional. The smoked wings I made for supper that evening were a success as well. What I have learned is that this grill is really a smoker. It does a great job for that purpose. Can you prepare a steak with it? Of course you can, but it isn't a replacement for a gas grill in my opinion, but instead a compliment to one. I will keep my gas grill for quick meals during the week and use my Traeger for smoking on the weekend.

title: Getting better
text: I had in issue with wi-fi.  Make sure customer service asks you what version you have.  I had one that was a day older that new version.  They send a replacement quickly.  Now I am enjoying using the wifi app with automatic menu down loads.  Very cool!  Still having issues with initial start up over heating and slow to move up or down temperatures as required for cook directions.  Getting better results each time I use it.  Thank you Traeger for moving me from not satisfied to happy!  I would now recommend this product.

title: Can't Beat Traeger
text: I got the pro 22 Sept. 2019 from QVC. Ten months later I was having a problem with the temp. causing the grill to go into HER. I called Traeger to buy a new LED controller, but found out my grill has a 3 year warranty, bumper to bumper. Wow if that doesn't say a lot for a company, I don't what does. The technician asked what it was doing and walked me through a troubleshooting to make sure of the fix. They sent me the new parts for free, no problems. Traeger grill makes regular guys, master BBQ guys. I live in Texas where brisket is king, my neighbors could believe  tender and how much flavor it had. This year I did my first Traeger turkey, my wife told me to throw my deep fryer away, she said that's the only way from now on. I've done pulled pork, whole chicken, and legs, and the ribs melt in your mouth. The only thing I'm going to change on my Traeger is, buy a bigger one in a year or so. Thanks Traeger!

title: No Smoke!
text: Don’t know why but I’m not getting smoke at low temps. Tried at 165,170 and 180. Disappointing for sure after spending $1000

title: Great versatile Cooker
text: Bought my Traeger Pro 34 around Late May 2020. Cooks great, ribs, butts, roasts and corned beef brisket.  Also have done corn on the cob. Only draw back, is now that the colder weather has set in I am having trouble locating an insulation blanket. They are out of stock everywhere. Other than that I love my Pro 34

title: Faulty Wi-Fi Controller
text:
I bought the grill and assembled it and the wi-fi feature will not work.  After reconfiguring my home wi-fi, the issue is still not resolved.  Traeger is sending me a new wi-fi controller, "hopefully" before Christmas, which is why we bought the grill in the first place.

I will not even season this grill unless this new wi-fi controller works, because I am not keeping it otherwise.

title: Wifi doesn’t connect
text: The grill is great but the biggest feature was the wifi and convenience that brings. The wifi won’t connect and the site says it might not be able to connect until February?! I believe I could’ve found a pellet grill without wifi for about half the price. I will change my rating if they get connected sooner, but it’s a hassle to have to run outside in 0 degree weather to check everything instead of just getting updated through the wifi feature.

title: Mr. Meat delivers!
text: It cooks so many different ways, I continue to develop my own style as well as use the wonderful recipes in the app. My 575 transports well in the back of my Tundra wherever I set up camp in my RV. I found out about Traeger when my brother got one for Fathers Day and he fixed the best pulled pork that I have ever had in my life! The recipe was already in the app with Cole slaw and everything else needed. Can’t recommend Traeger enough!

title: I love this smoker
text: Purchased the Ironwood 885 for smoking a 20 lb Thanksgiving turkey and a boatload of stuffing.  Everything came out great.  The temperature control on this smoker amazing and the app makes controlling the smoker easy without having to go outside.  I also have an older Pro Series 575 (before it was called the 575) and there is no comparison between the smokers (not that there is anything wrong with the Pro Series, I love that smoker too and plan on using both for cook-outs this summer).  So glad I upgraded.

title: these grills suck

title: Best present my wife ever bought me.
text: I have nothing but good things to say about this smoker. Not only does everything i cook on it come out great but it's super easy to clean. Every time I cook on it the entire neighborhood gets jealous weather it's in the summer or winter. A Traeger will be the only smoker/grill I own for life.

title: Why did I wait?

title: Not a smoker!

This is a very good Grill, but a very poor smoker. Very disappointed. I already want to sell it. I didn’t need a grill! I am so bugged!

title: This Grill has been Awesome!
text: If you can afford it, you won't regret it.  Definitely the best chicken I've ever made repeatedly. Whether smoked or grilled, every recipe has come out awesome.  I make sure I vacuum out the ashes every 4-5 uses, but not necessary that often. Still need to try to smoke a brisket, but waiting for warmer days for that.

title: Horrible WiFire & Customer Service
text: We bought the Timberline 1300 around thanksgiving due in part to its slick WiFire app marketing. Well, buyer beware: so many people are bashing the WiFi experience online in the forums and in the App comments. Traeger’s customer service points the finger at your home mesh network and entourages you to buy a 2.4 signal router. title: Pretty good
text: This thing is awsome of course you have to mess with it every once in a while nothings perfect and last forever

title: Love The Grill When It Works
text:
I purchased Timberline 1300 from our local ACE Hardware in March of 2020.
A couple months after it started having issues.  Lots of smoke coming out of the Hopper.  So they sent me a replacement fan. The unit still constantly has startup issues and trouble getting to temp or slow ignite errors. They have now sent a new heating rod.  I'm waiting on ACE to come replace the parts. The back of the grill is also rusting out so they sent a new back cover. For $2,000 I should not be having so many issues. I tried to use the grill last night and the temp went up to almost 600 then got high heat error and the grill went into shutdown mode. The inconsistency of this grill has messed up Thanksgiving Dinner & Birthday Parties for our family.  When its working it is great but I'm wondering every time I turn it on if it's going to work.  God knows how many bags of pellets have been wasted.  Tech supports reply is usually empty the hopper and put fresh pellets in. Support has been good about sending parts but doesn't seem to care beyond that.  I've even had to call back to request work orders for the repair.  Support says that most people do the repairs themselves.  That maybe true but for $2,000 and still under warranty why should I have to constantly take it apart.

title: Traeger
text: I always check reviews before making a purchase on anything. So to my much surprise when checking the reviews. I found that any complaint that was made on this product was answered by support. Due to this simple fact I will be purchasing one of these grill. Never have I seen a company answer hardly any reviews. To see the company answer and be so willing to help real good keep up the good work.

title: Terrible paint quality very disappointed
text: I was crazy in low with my traeger pro 575. I have had my traeger for a little over a year and from putting it together to smoking to grilling the thing worked like a charm and I was immensely satisfied. New Years Eve I fire up my Traeger set it to 500 to make wood fire pizzas. Family is all excited I have 6 pies all lined up ready to go and all of a sudden there’s a metallic burning smell in kitchen. I look out my back door to see the paint on my Traeger melting off I look at the temp dial and it says it’s only at 400. I quickly run outside begin the shut down process open up the traeger don’t notice anything out of the usual. I called customer service and spent 45 minutes on the phone with this nice girl trying to explain to her that paint should not be melting and flaking off a grill. She was very nice but did not seem interested in helping me get to the bottom of my problem and chalked it up to being a grease or pellet fire and there was nothing she can do. I’m worried to even turn my grill on again and worried about melting paint and that paint turning to dust on my unit and she just kept asking me how I enjoy my traeger and what I have cooked on it and what I am going to cook in the future on it. I tried to tell her how disappointed I am with how this call is going so she put me on two 5-10 holds. Finally she comes back and says there is still nothing she can do about the body of my grill but has order me some interior pieces for my unit. I’m writing this review to advise people to think twice about buying a 800 dollar grill that when you cook on it the possibility of melting of the exterior will happen. Not sure I will be cooking on my unit again a lot of money poured down the drain because paint is turning to dust and that doesn’t seem safe to have food around that and to consume.

title: Timberline 850 junk

title: Best purchase ever made!

title: Awesome Grill / Smoker

title: Pro 34

title: So disappointed

title: Stop contemplating and do it!

title: Easy as “set it and forget it”

title: Never Again

title: I love the Ironwood 885
text: I cant believe I didn’t get one of these years ago. Very easy to put together and set up. Indirect heat plus wood pellets makes it very easy to cook great chicken and fish. I have a big green egg and a WSM but the Ironwood and my blackstone will be what I use for the majority of my cooking.

title: This work horse will change your life
text: Y'all, I cannot hardly put into words how much my wife and I love our 885 Ironwood. The versatility, the convenience, most importantly that Traeger TASTE! I promise you wont go wrong with this one.

title: Safety hazard - catches fire easily

title: Good smoker, trash WiFi

title: Taking cooking to the next level.

I’ve made brisket, pulled pork, ribs,  smoked salmon, and my own bacon.  It was all amazing!  With smoking, it takes cooking to another level.  You get flavor that you can’t get with a regular grill.

title: Do Not Buy This Grill
text: Before you buy a Traeger, google “traeger will not hold temperature”. There you’ll find groups of people troubleshooting what should be a premium product. To their credit, the customer service people are always polite, but you shouldn’t drop almost 800 bucks on a grill and get to know the customer service people so well you’re thinking you should send them Xmas cards. If you like laying on the cold ground, week after week, part after part, replacing core components that should work out of the box, this is the grill for you. I heat my house with basically the same size pellet auger and fire pot and I can’t get this to the temp that many of their own recipes call for.

title: Biggest waste of money ever
text:
This is not a bbq pit, this is like a air fryer and oven had a baby.
0 smoke flavor, will not get hot enough to sear anything. Even in cast iron with oil

title: Damaged Right Out Of The Box
text: Decided to buy the 2018 Pro Series based on my desire to finally try a Traeger smoker and the seemed like a really good deal...big mistake!!! After setting it up, I noticed it had some crush damage with exposed wiring during delivery. I went online expecting Traeger would arrange for the repair, but instead learned I would have to register my newly purchased (& also broken) T raeger and find my own repair service. I can’t wait how fun it will be to try to get parts for a 2018 Traeger smoker!!!

title: Owner No Smoke Flavor  Ironwood 885 Pellet Grill
text: I bought this about 5 months ago, and have tried all kinds of different type and brands of pellets, barely get any smoke flavor with the super smoke feature, ive tried temps at 165 to 225 and nothing. maybe part of the reason is i went from a charcoal smoker to this Ironwood 885 Pellet Grill. I'm Very disappointed in this purchase, I will probably go back to the charcoal/ wood smoker.. Hope this helps anyone thinking about this Ironwood 885 Pellet Grill

title: Love it!
text: I just got this grill 3 wks ago and it is GREAT! Still learning the hot spots but it’s going to work well for my catering business!!!

title: Very happy with this smoker
text: Expensive?  Yes, kind of..  Most expensive grill I've bought? Nope.  Quality and satisfaction?  Spot on, and I'm not the easiest to please.  I've called twice with minor questions and both times have been quite impressed with service and a short wait time.  You WILL need 2 people at the end of assembly to set the smoker upright but moves around on the wheels pretty decent.  The app for the wifi is great.  Get yourself a cheap or used shop-vac to keep it clean (I'm weird that way, sue me).  The cover they offer is the best I've ever seen, worth every penny even though I keep mine indoors most of the time.

title: Wish We Could Brag About This Grill
text: We purchased this grill in September 2019.  It worked fantastic the first six months.  After that we have had nothing but problems and the grill has only operated about two months since our first issue.  We have contacted support and they have tried to help us.  They have sent 3 controllers and a power cord but the unit will not come on.  The last conversation was in January 22, 2021 and they were going to send another part.  We have not received it or any communication regarding it.  We really enjoy the grill - on the rare occasions it works.  Unfortunately we can not recommend it.   I'd think twice before buying this grill.  Nothing but a disappointment.

title: WOW
text: After using a Traeger Junior for 2 years I decided to move up to an Ironwood 650. It was like moving from a camp stove to a full gourmet kitchen. Temperature is precise and the extra smoke feature is great. Having the Wifire app makes cooking super easy. Now I can relax while the Traeger does the work. I haven’t gotten into the different programs yet but even without them the capabilities of the Ironwood series is amazing.

title: Makes great food, but the thermostat is garbage
text: I’ve owned this for just about a year and have smoked and cooked all kinds of meats on it. Every time they come out great. However, since about the 3rd or 4th month, the thermostat has never read the correct temperature, not even close. At any given time it can read 190 or read 500 and it can go back and forth in a split second. I gave up on that part of it and just use an IR thermometer and adjust the setting until I’m close to what I want. Sometimes it just shuts down. I don’t know why. If it didn’t smoke things so well it would get 1 star, but that’s the one thing it does actually do. I probably won’t  buy another Traeger, when this one finally dies, however.

title: Great performance but very poor QC on finish
text: Bought this yesterday used it for some light cooking. Liked the super smoke feature like the even heating and very spacious cooking area back draft exhaust is definitely the future of smokers. So the biggest problem I have with this grill is the finishing on the stainless steel part's. It's atrocious and for what I paid that's just unacceptable and makes me think if they couldn't bother with proper finishing techniques where else have they cut corners on this smoker. And I found it this Smoker is only tack welded no complete welds they sealed it with RTV and mine already leaks out of the box from a corner of the barrel. I will either return this and buy a Yoder. Or maybe fix traeger's mistakes.

title: Wifi app doesn't work, not really any smoke flavor
text:
Never could get the wifi app to connect after working with customer service. So it never did any of the updates and the grill would never get up to 500 degrees like advertised. 

I don't know if most people that buy these things don't have any idea what good bbq or smoked meat is like but this is severally lacking. It's basically just an outdoor oven an neither a grill nor a smoker. I used several bags of Traeger's wood pellets too to try and see if I could get a good smoke flavor and never did. makes sense why you see smoking instruction videos use the better grill models with "super smoke".  I gave it two stars instead of one because it has the potential there with all the features, just poorly executed. Maybe stop spending all of your budget on marketing and making yourselves look like Yeti of the grilling world and put some money into the electronics. If you just google "wifi connection problem treager" you will get pages and pages of complaints.

title: Best Birthday Present Ever!
text:
My wife bought this for me for my Birthday.  What a great gift to both of us! A whole new way to cook - but the App and Traeger Forum give you tons of guidance, great ideas, recipes to get started. Also many great YouTube sessions on all manner of brisket, rubs, etc.  We've done pizza, wings, ribs, etc.  No:  Is it Too Hot?  Is it Too Cold?, no flareup incinerations, no running out of gas (app tells you if you're running low on pellets plenty early).  Just even steady heat at the temp you choose.   Only hard thing was when I started it up the other day and it told me I had to wait - it was doing a software update over the WiFi.  My Weber NEVER did that!   ;-)

P.S.  If you buy it from your local Ace Hardware- most will assemble and deliver for free.  Not hard to do yourself - but for free?  Great Price!

P.S.

title: Buy a cheaper model instead
text: As a hole I would say pellet smokers work really good but I  would hesitate before buying a Timberline series from a dealer. I bought my Timberline 850 from one of Traeger's platinum dealers and since people buy the lower end ones so much more then the high end models this one had sat in the show room too long and had out dated software in the D-2 controler. Traeger made me re-connect to the grill over and over again for a week and a half before they finally would send me a new controller but instead of sending it express shipping they gentleman said I have to wait another week or more to get the part I need. That will mean my BRAND NEW TIMBERLINE 850 won't even work properly for the first 3 WEEKS that I will have owned it. Save your money and just buy a pro series the extra you spend on the top end Traeger grills doesn't matter to Traeger at all they won't work harder to help you out and if I bought a pro series instead I would be one of their happy customers enjoy my fully working grills instead.

title: Very Disappointed
text: Spent a thousand dollars on a second Traeger and within months its chipping paint? It has 10 feet of cover so no rain can hit it. Completely unacceptable. Traeger pro 780

title: Unbelievable grill that lets you cook like a pro!

title: Best Grill I've ever owned!
text: I got my Ironwood 650 about 3 weeks ago and I'm absolutely obsessed with it!  I've made both the best ribs and the best brisket I've ever made, as well as multiple burgers, hotdogs, and sausages.  Up next is pulled pork! title: Buy a different grill if you want the WiFi feature

title: DO NOT BUY!

title: Never Going Back
text:
I've been grilling for years...on charcoal, with gas,  wood chips, you name it. I got the Pro Series 22 and will never go back, only look forward to what I can create next.

I live in Calif. and use my Traeger 3-4 times per week, for just about a year now and it's like new.  Be sure to use your shop vac to clean out the pellet dust in the bottom of the burner every other time you use it. Otherwise, the temp doesn't come all the way up to 450. It's simple to do though-takes two minutes. 

If you are thinking about anything else, STOP!  This is the Do-All/End-All grill. It's not just for smoking. I crank it up for hamburgers, hot dogs, Carne Asada, searing meats and it turns out way better than any grill I've ever owned. title: This Grill Makes Me a Meat Hero!

title: First impressions are everything...( not so great)
text:
So I finally pulled the trigger on a Traeger.... I picked up a brand new 780 pro Gen2 this weekend at my local ACE (5/08/21). After I followed the pre first cook instructions(seasoning and 450 burn for 30 min) I decided to do ribs for my first cook at 225, and to my surprise they were not done at the 5 hr mark (3 smoking, 2 wrapped in foil)!? Done this method many times without fail. Internal temp on the ribs was only at 180!? So I decided to test the ambient temp of the grill with my ThermoWorks smoke probe and come to find out, the grill was off by 40 degrees!? I then got my old Redi Check probe out and that also read 40 degrees lower than what the Traeger was telling me. This definitely explains why the ribs were not done. I was only smoking at around 180 - 185 degrees apparently. 

So I called support and they are sending me a replacement Thermocouple. I really hope this solves the issue, this is the most money I've ever spent on a grill and for it to not work better than my 22" weber kettle I've been using for the last 10 yrs is, to say the least, extremely disappointing. If this does not work I will be returning for a full refund.
 
I will update my review once I receive the part and do some testing.

title: Very Disappointed. Paint pealed after 3 months
text:
Bought an Ironwood 650 expecting it to last me years to come. I was wrong!!!  After 3 months the paint began pealing!!  I called fully expecting Traeger to stand behind their product and I was wrong again.  After talking to multiple people from Traeger they all gave me the same line of "The grill got too hot and clean your grill more".  For the record I did clean my grill regularly and it was always covered or in the garage out of the weather! I have a 20 year old Weber Grill that has been screeching hot, flames billowing, and never pealed paint! If a grease fire is potentially the cause then you are always just one grease flare-up from pealing paint!?  Their fix for the problem is for me to go to my local hardware store and buy high temp grill paint and touchup the spots.... a 3 month old $1200 grill, just "hit it with a little spray paint!?"  

Do your research.  Other people on forums have had the same problem I have had in the same spot of the grill. I have a friend that was about to pull the trigger on a Traeger and I will be convincing him otherwise.

Such a shame.  Fun to cook on, food tastes great, but their quality has slipped and they are not willing to stand behind their product.

title: Great Cooking
text: I've had my Traeger Pro for a year now and I have zero regrets. It has proven time and again that it is super simple to use and easy to keep clean. I get great food every time I use it and it never fails to impress. Worth every penny to us.

title: Not with the money.

title: Wild fluctuations on a 72 degree day
text: Its 72 degrees out, vacuumed out my traeger of ash, used pellets, and cleaned out the grease (which I do before every cook).  Started it up on smoke, once smoking, set the temp to 225, to smoke a brisket. Over the course of my cook, I saw it go all the way to 198, and all the way up to 298.  Traeger says +/- 25 is normal....I could deal with that!! But a variance of 73 degrees is NOT acceptable.  I called Traeger after I first bought this last summer and it was doing wild fluctuations then....they told me me it could be the weather (too hot), the foil on the grease pan (I made sure it was nice and flat against the pan), Ive always cleaned it before every cook....Im really tired of these fluctuations...Im starting to wonder seriously about this smoker!  Buyer beware.

title: Awesome

title: Love the flavors
text: I purchased this for myself as a birthday gift about a year ago. Great quality and pretty much does as described. As with others, I have occasionally had temperature fluctuations and one incident of pellets burnt in the auger at the fire box. After doing my research and following instructions provided by Traeger, I discovered that the pellets that were left in the hopper and auger had adsorbed just a touch of the ambient humidity during a rare damp period (I live in the SW desert). I replaced the pellets and everything works very well. I use the grill cover religiously and leave as few pellets as possible in the hopper/auger as a pop-up storm during the monsoon season could be an issue. I love the flavor blends in the Traeger pellets and have smoked/grilled just about every kind of meat, poultry, and fish as well as select veggies. The cleanup can be a bit of a pain with needing to shop vac out the residue after each use but overall love this product.

title: Perfect Baby Back Ribs 1st Try!!!

title: Cons

title: Very Disappointed
text:

title: Not happy

title: It's a Traeger - Not a Grill
text: I purchased my Pro 575 a few weeks ago and I'm really enjoying it.  The assy was very simple and I only needed help to roll it over onto all four.  TIP - Use some masking tape and securely tape the door and hopper lid so that they don't fly open during assy.  Overall it took about an hour to assemble.  I moved on to the seasoning of the Traeger and it went just as in the manual.  Since then I've smoked some ribeyes and made a blackberry cobbler.  I now have a rack of baby back ribs on low and slow (3-2-1) and the Traeger is performing excellently after 2 hours into the cook.  I love the Traeger app even though I'm still learning how to use features such as the cook now in the recipes.  I've also swapped out the Signature for the Hickory pellets for my ribs.  That was very easy using the trap door.  I also used a wooden spoon to push the remaining pellets out into the bucket.  Then just topped it off with hickory pellets and on my way.  TIP - Purchase an HD Homer bucket and lid to store pellets in and help with swapping pellets.  Overall the cooking process has been very simple and I enjoy being able to check on my Traeger from my couch using the app.  I am looking into a searing plate to help sear steaks.  Even at 450F the sear wasn't quite what I like on my steaks and the sear plate will help with that.  Overall, I do recommend the Pro 575.  It has everything I want without all of the bells and whistles AND WiFire.  Just remember it's a Traeger and not your run of the mill grill.  Do your research to understand what a Traeger is compared to a grill to help with your purchase.  All in all you won't be disappointed in the Traeger.

title: Awesome product!

title: assembly advice
text: I just bought the Timberline 850 and after quite a bit of research on pellet grills.  I was originally going to buy the Ironwood 650 but once I was at the store a decided to go all in with the timberline 850.  I am a pretty meticulous guy that pays attention to detail.  I was so excited to assemble my grill and use it for the first time on Saturday.  I watched assembly videos on line and also read the book prior to assembling my grill.  I followed the instructions but there is one key point I would like to make.  Both the video and the instructions tell you to lay the grill down on the cardboard box to make it easier to attach the legs.  I took the advice along with the advice to use part of the packaging to elevate the grill a little before attaching the legs.  I did just that and what they don't tell you is to make sure you secure the lid for the grill and the pellet bin.  When I elevated the bottom just 2-3 inches both lids came open and banged into the brick patio floor.  I was sick, I had not even assembled my grill yet and and the finish was already damaged.  It took quite a bit of excitement out of the process and when I was cooking on it that afternoon all I could do was look at the scuffs and shake my head.  The food turned out great but I am totally frustrated out about the scuffs on the lids.  Please make sure you secure them prior to propping up the grill for leg attachment.

title: WIFI Issues as always
text:
I bought this Timberline Series 850 about 2 months ago and until now I CAN'T CONNECT TO MY HOME WIFI despite several calls to the Customer service! Luckily, I can still use it (manually) without the fancy phone/wifi connections. 

This pellet "grill" is actually a SMOKER and NOT a gas or charcoal grill replacement! Don't believe those people who claim to achieve sear marks on their steaks with this! Cleaning  before every use is also very important! Otherwise, you'll have flare ups particularly if using high temperature cooking. The paint in the back where the vents are located is already chipping after 2 uses (including the seasoning step)! This is not acceptable at all for this price range!

The smoking capability of this pricey smoker is so so. You cannot use this for creating "rushed" dinner after work! Slow day long cooking probably is where this unit shines. I ended up buying another gas grill to suit my needs (and I was dead wrong about using this pellet grill as a regular gas grill replacement!). I've been using wood chips to my natural gas grill for decades now and it worked for me. Buying this expensive "toy" was a mistake!

In summary, do yourself a favor and research carefully before venturing into the pellet grill bandwagon! Don't make the same mistake I did and review those numerous reviews about wifi connectivity issues and suboptimal paint jobs! If given another chance, I would probably buy the cheaper smoker that uses real wood chips! Goodluck!

title: Low quality, poor design, high price
text: We were so excited to upgrade to a Timberline 1300 last week after having a Lil Tex Elite for 8 years and loving it.  Our excitement quickly turned to disappointment and frustration with the very first use.  We live in an area of Wyoming where winters are long and cold, so we were very excited about the double wall insulation of the Timberline 1300.  The insulation and the door gasket are somewhat defeated though by the fact that the door doesn't close all of the way.  I'm also very disappointed that when we rolled the grill to move it one of the wheels fell off and all of the bearings came out, so now our brand new almost $2,000 grill is propped up with a block of wood.  The icing on top of the cake is that Trager claims that the Timberline 1300 will cook 6 pork butts at a time.  This is very true for grill space, but the grease system is only sized for 3.  On our first and only cook we cooked six pork butts.  We started with a new empty liner, but I came around the corner half way through the cook to a huge puddle of grease on the concrete under the grill.  When the grill cooled and I was able to investigate I found that the liner had filled completely and run over  into the tray and then all over the concrete.  The timberline seemed like such an upgrade over our Lil Tex Elite, but so far only the controller seems better, and that was not worth the price.

title: Very disappointing
text:
Very disappointed after having had the Pro 575 for almost six weeks and used 2 - 3 times per week. 
1) The temperatures fluctuate heavily more than 10 degrees Celsius and has resulted in dried out food on every low and slow cook (no it is not due to frequently opening the grill - only as per app recipe steps to spritz). Apparently this is actually a know issue by Traeger yet to be resolved by config.
2) large amounts of ash are produced and leave residue on the food, grates and grill opening (this was from the start and the grill is cleaned after EVERY use)
3) Grill Temperature sensor has already lost it's coating
4) Very little smoke is produced and can hardly be tasted (yes I understand the difference between white and blue smoke and yes this was on low / slow cooking)

The Pro 575 clearly needs the super smoke function and needs better configuration to handle the temperature variations.

title: A lot of medium sized irks eventually add up
text:
Pretty disappointed with my grill…not but a couple of months old and I’ve finally had enough medium issues that I’m pretty upset with the way this has been performing. My reason for choosing Traeger was I thought I was paying more for quality and durability, though I’ve found this is incorrect. I’ll also let it be known I’ve never written a one star review, pretty bummed this has to be my first.

I’d like to think I take care of my stuff, and very well too. I regularly clean my grill and replace my drip pans, I keep my pellets store in a dry shed, I cover my grill after every cook, all to protect its longevity…. But this hasn’t proven to help much. 

First is my biggest complaint. Today, for the 4th time my grill has started smoking up in the pellet box, not the grill. I had plenty of pellets, and went outside to check the box multiple times- even making sure they were feeding correctly (because I’ve had this issue before a few times) but when set at 250 after not checking on it for about 30 mins I went out to see my grill at 341 degrees and the pellet box smoking like crazy, while my pork was cool enough to handle. I’ve had this before a few times but today has happened 3 times!! After each time I shut it down, put the meat in the oven, let the grill cool off for an hour at least, put it back on and after about an hour it starts messing up again. Very frustrating.

Second- my grill paint is bubbling/chipping. I’ve seen many other reviews on this. I’ve never had a grease fire, nor have I used max heat other than a handful of times… and I keep my grill covered when not in use, so that’s clearly an issue.

Lastly- just to paint a picture about my current frustrations with the Traeger brand… about 1/3 of my pellet bag is bad. I keep my bags off the floor in my shed and this was a brand new unopened bag that was bad… this is the second time I’ve gotten a bag with bad chips… the last time wasn’t quite as much though- this being a third of my bag at least though proved a much bigger annoyance. 

I have many friends with Traegers with positive experiences, unfortunately mine isn’t great. Just beware I guess… inspect your bags to the best extent and be careful to watch your pellet box. Definitely don’t want that thing catching mid cook. I’ve attached a few pictures, unfortunately didn’t think to snag a pic of the box smoking.

title: No, no, and no. Stay away!!!
text:
I’ve had this grill now for about 3 months and have only used it twice so far. The setup of the grill is pretty self explanatory with the direction guidebook and definitely beneficial to have a couple extra hands to help out to streamline the process. Setting up the wi-fire app was a total breeze as well. Before starting your first cook on the grill, they advise you to ‘season’ the smoker and the directions are provided as well.

Anyway, moving onto the cooking. Relatively a good smoker. My first time smoking, I would say the internal temperature inside the grill remained roughly 10-15 degrees higher or lower at times based on the temperature that I set. Apparently this is pretty standard. It wasn’t until my second time when I noticed that the internal temperature was extremely off. I would set my smoker on the low setting of 180 degrees, and the internal temperature would be sticking around 200-250 degrees!!! I had to ultimately set the grill on it’s lowest temp of 165 degrees for the smoker to continuously stay around the 200-230 area. I called Traeger and they believe its due to the thermocouple… so they sent me a new replacement. What the heck?! After the second cook and I’m already having to replace something? Also, the inside of my smoker has PAINT CHIPPING. I also notified Traeger about this and they believe that there was a fire inside of the smoker which had caused this to happen. They claim that this is not “common” but they can’t do anything about it. What an absolute joke! I paid $1,000+ and I’m stuck with a grill that had paint chipping inside and a messed up thermocouple after two times of usage!!!! What the heck. I do not recommend this grill to anyone.

title: Abysmal quality and value
text: I was on the market for a Pellet grill and I went straight to Traeger top of the line grill without making any research just based on their reputation and popularity. The Timberline 850 is an absolute failure in terms of quality and design and I'm saying this based on not one, but two grills as I was sent a replacement in hopes that the issues I found were not systemic. The grill paint will start to bubble and come off as soon as you do your first burn in and the heat probe inside the chamber is a flimsy almost loose wire, absolutely unacceptable if you compare that to the quality of the probes from many comparable grills even in a cheaper price range. The drip tray covers do not even remotely close fit the size of the actual drip tray and they melt immediately upon heating. Generally speaking, it's clear that there are a ton of bad design decision and corner cutting in the quality of the production. This grill is worth maybe 800$, not 2000$. A RecTec, just to name one of several better alternatives, is in every way superior to this grill for a cheaper price. Ultimately, in Traeger's defense, they did stand by their product and accepted a return and a full refund outside of the 30-day window which was commendable and appreciated.

title: Regret
text:
Writing this review after 6 months of use…. I will simply say that I regret spending so much money on this smoker. It does everything as advertised, and is very easy to use, but before you buy it you need to know that you cannot cook at the 500 degree setting as advertised. Do yourself a favor and Google search the number of complaints about paint chipping on these models.

In my 6 months, I have only taken it above 400 degrees twice (the initial recommended burn in and for one cook). After the second time, it caused the paint to bubble, chip, and peel. I contacted customer support because the metal is now exposed, which could eventually lead to rust or worse a hole, but I was told that it was my fault the paint chipped away. They said my pictures appear to have too much grease build up, assumed I had a fire in the pit, and therefore they would not replace the unit because paint isn’t covered under warranty… I’ll let you judge for yourselves about the amount of grease build up in the photos I’ve posted.

In conclusion, I absolutely love the ease of use with this smoker, but I wish I had purchased a competitor smoker for $500 and not had the regret of investing so much money in this unit. I thought I would pay a lot up front and buy a smoker that would last for several years, but now I have to live with doubt that my investment will hold up. So before making this purchase, do your homework and know that customer service will not stand by paint defects.

title: Disappointed
text:
I’ve owned my Pro 34 for less than three months and have used it three times.  The first cook went well.  During the second cook the temperature swings were crazy.  I had it set at 180, and the swings went from 90 to 315.  I called Traeger and they figured the problem was likely the RTD sensor (temperature sensor).  They promptly sent me a replacement.  The instructions to replace it were pretty simple and I had no issues changing the part.

Yesterday I fired up the grill for a third time.  Temperature set at 180.  For the first Three hours the temperature fluctuated between 175 and 220.  While this is a big swing, I can live with it.  After hour 3, the temperature went to 280-295 and was not dropping.  I decided to just turn off the grill.

This is a three month old pellet grill.  Why is it my responsibility to change parts on the grill?  I believe Traeger should figure out a way to do that for me.  And, I still have the temperature problem.  Not quite sure what to do at this point.  I am very good about not opening the lid, and I purchased the Traeger insulation blanket.

Thus far, I am very disappointed in this product.

title: Awesome Grill!!!!

The wifire was a cinch to set up and I can use it to monitor cooking temp and meat temp while at work or on the golf course.  It's held up well even though it's used 2-3 times/week and for long cooks on weekends, 18 hours sometimes.  The only problem has been a worn-out fire pot which Traeger quickly replaced under warranty.  Everything else has held up well including the paint.  My only complaint is that tar/cresote will build up on the bottom edge of the grill door - you have to constantly clean this area or it will dribble down the outside of the tub and onto the ground.  Seems like a lip could be incorporated into the door to catch this residue and drain it to the inside.  I've cooked everything from pork but, brisket, ribs, roasts, tenderloins, whole chickens, fish and veggies and everything comes out perfectly cooked with a delicious BBQ flavor.  The grill will give you a very good smoke ring and poppers come out perfect.  You can get a reasonable sear on steaks although I still tend to use my egg for steaks as I like to sear directly over coals.  Overall, this will be your go-to grill and it will give you awesome tasting cooks.

title: Please read before you buy this model.
text:
I wasn't going to write this review, but it seems the only way to contact the company discreetly is by phone, so now I'm just going to go ahead and make this public. There is one important thing you should know about this particular model if you're planning to buy it.

Due to the design of the pellet feed auger assembly, there is a good possibility you will have to replace this part at-least once on this grill. The specific part number is "KIT0020" You can look that up and find it's general availability where you live. This auger drive motor and gear box is essentially free-floating off the end of the auger and due to this, it is very likely to get "bound up" destroying the small gears inside it's pot-metal gearbox. I'm not an engineer by trade but have taken a lot of things apart to fix them and this just blew my mind. Maybe this is a manufacturer defect and somebody forgot to install something on the assembly line but there are no detents or witness marks to indicate where a part should be installed or holes should be drilled etc. There is nothing holding the motor and gearbox in the proper place. It is allowed to turn around the auger shaft several degrees before the corner of the gearbox comes in contact with another metal fitment inside the housing. There's no little rubber stopper or anything there to indicate they intended the motor to be loose like this or anything else to indicate thought was put into building it this way.

This replacement part is not an expensive one, but you do have to take the entire feed pellet system apart and remove it from the grill to get to this motor. This means carefully removing wires and remembering where they go. Fortunately about half of them have the plugs marked with colored stickers that are *Almost* the same color so you can hope that's where that wire goes. It's just mains voltage so no biggie for a home gamer.

Having gone to several stores in my area to track down this elusive part 24 hours before I intend to cook a turkey in this grill, I have gotten a chance to see literally all of the other, newer versions of the auger feed system that Traeger has designed and put on the market. They are all much more sophisticated. Almost like entirely different engineers designed them.

If this was not a one off manufacturer defect, this grill needs to be recalled so the above design flaw can be fixed. This could also be remedied by designing a retrofit that owners of this model of grill could install to prevent the motor from being damaged. At no cost to the consumer.

If you still decide you want to get this model, at least now you know what to expect and what to look for.

title: Terrible Experience
text:
This is my 3rd review.  I bought the Pro-34 in late August and have had nothing but problems.  Temperature control being the main one.  I replaced the temperature probe.  That did not work.  Ace Hardware (great service on their part) then replaced the hot rod.  That did not fix my problem.  Ace then replaced the control module.  No luck.  Traeger then authorized replacement of the pellet box assembly (the entire mechanical part operation...all three of the above parts).  Today I did my first cook with the new pellet box assembly.  Still had temperature swings of 80+ degrees.  And, after 2 hours, it simply stopped working when set at 180.  No smoke and no heat.  When it got to 90 degrees I shut it off, emptied the pellet box (to make sure the auger wasn't clogged), and started the cook again.  Set it at 225 and got heat and smoke.  Set it back to 180, and the same thing happened.... no heat or smoke.  Shut it down and repeated the process.  Nothing.  The smoker simply would not work at 180.  So... I set it at 225 and tried to monitor the beef jerky.  Unfortunately, I pretty much ruined 4.5 pounds of eye round.  

I will not use this smoker again.  I am going to attempt to get my money back tomorrow (I know.... good luck) and buy a different brand of smoker.

Don't get me wrong, everyone (Traeger and Ace) has been wonderful to work with.  Everyone has tried to get this straightened out.  Unfortunately, with the grill, cover, and insulation blanket, I'm into this for a bit under $1,000 and have had nothing  but flat our frustration.

title: Don’t buy!
text: Do yourself and don’t buy this grill or any traeger product. Look elsewhere for higher quality less known brands. I wish I would have. My grill shuts off mid cook all the time deliver LER errors. Troubleshoot with traeger, Facebook, YouTube Reddit…. Tons of people with same issue. Smoke a pork butt or brisket overnight? Want to run an errand for an hour? Good luck. Your traeger will be similar to a 2 year old. You can’t leave it alone or take your eye off it or next thing you know it will shut off and your $100 piece of meat will be spoiled. Try to exchange it and upgrade for one with wifire? Traeger won’t stand by their product and you’ll be in a never ending rotation of replacement parts. Traegers are the Kias of the smoker world. Good luck.

title: If you’re thinking about it… Buy it!
text: I honestly can’t believe some of the negative reviews on this grill. Everything that I’ve seen negative makes me scratch my head. I’ve had this grill about a month and have made some pulled pork which was to die for and some of the best Tri-Tip that I’ve ever had in my life. This grill has plenty of smoke, the Wi-Fi feature and app is incredible. I upgraded from a grill that didn’t have the Wi-Fi feature and i couldn’t be happier with my purchase. I hope everybody that is thinking about buying this grill pulls the trigger! Get ready for some of the best BBQ of your life.

title: Disappointed
text: I’ve spent more time fixing my Traeger then actually cooking with it. Had to replace so many components on my own. Customer service does a good job but it seems their answer is send you more parts. Had people over for the football game yesterday and had to use my old Webber…when it works it works great but be ready to be disappointed!

title: Good not Great
text: I've had my timberline for a little over a year now.  I do love how my food turns out.  Everything is amazing and there is nothing better than to set it and forget it and go enjoy a beer while it slow cooks my ribeye to perfection.  However, I do have one beef with it.  I feel like the Grease Management System is faulty, Even though my drip tray is installed correctly it doesn't seem to angle enough towards the front.  Like the brackets in the back need to be higher.  Everytime I cook the grease piles up on the sides of my drip tray so if I'm mid cook and I need to up the temperature to sear something I can catch my grill on fire because nothing is draining properly.  I feel the system that they have on other models is a far better way to take care of grease and because of that I'm going to be purchasing an Ironwood soon.  I still love Traeger and I will be a forever customer of their's.  The Timberline is just not for me sadly.

title: New BBQ Broken Parts
text:
We purchased this BBQ new, immediately the BBQ started malfunctioning and turning off mid cooking. The lights were glitching out like there was a short in the connection somewhere. I pulled the control panel out and the soldering was never completed, I temporarily smashed the soldering together to help make a connection again. 

I contacted Traeger, they refused to help in any way. They wanted a picture of the problem and I sent it to them when it shut off. Nothing. This was brand new out of the box. I've been battling them for awhile now and no help. I would purchase something from a different pellet BBQ company that cares about customer service more.

title: Love my Traeger grill
text: I'm writing a review on my smoker and would like to make a couple comments. A Traeger grill, when kept properly cleaned will produce the most wonderful results that are humanly possible when smoking meats. My next-door neighbor has a stand-up,  4 rack smoker that cooks with wood chips (not pellets) that you must attend the entire time that you're cooking. If you are seeking to achieve a very heavily charred deep deep smoky taste, then you own the wrong grill. The only way you're going to achieve that rich (wood taste) is with a manual add your own chips smoker. Yes my neighbors meat when cooked turns out completely different than mine both in looks and taste. Definitely not a look or taste that we desire. My entire family and friends have attended our cook outs and everyone chooses our well balanced flavor that my wonderful Traeger produces. I'm not writing this because anyone has influenced me or enticed me to do so. Smoking meat properly will leave you with the taste of spices, sauces and meat in a balanced nature. Now my neighbors results are so high in smoke flavor that you don't have that balance at all. You taste smoke with everything else not tasting the way it was intended to taste. This will probably be taken down but in case it doesn't, I speak the truth. I prefer that my meat has the flavors that are true to their intended flavors with the lovely smoke flavor married to it. Not tasting like wood.Thomas

title: 1300 T.Horrible grill! Catches fire all the time!
text: I have less than a year with the grill, it seems to catch fire every other smoke I do. Yes, I have cleaned and vacuumed the grill prior to any start up to prevent that issue from happening. I also scrap any grease and replace the liner but nothing seems to work!  It has ruined multiple cooks, it’s disappointing since it cost so much money! Such a waste!

title: I love it

title: BEST GRILL/COMPANY EVER!!!
text: I bought my Traeger approximately a year ago. After a year of experimenting and competing locally with friends. I would recommend Traeger grills & products to everyone. I used their Vic’s toner support for some basic questions reference their products. Customer support was quick, accommodating, and friendly!

title: Best cooking I have ever done
text: I purchased my Pro 575 before the pandemic began, so about 2.5 years ago. It has definitely done everything I had hoped. I have cooked the traditional steaks, shrimp, etc. that I always did and the only difference is the initial sear I can't get like you can from other frills. But the grill does so much more!!! Then she called me back and walked me through it for 30 mins step by step. I had never seen customer support like that before. I am definitely a loyal customer as long as the company continues to show values like that.

title: Great purchase
text: I bought the Ironwood 885 a couple months ago and absolutely love it. The WiFi connected easily(read directions). I’ve smoked whole chickens and ribs and came out outstanding. Still learning on using as a grill also but am very happy with it. Simple to clean also.

title: Very happy with my iron wood
text: I find every excuse to smoke on the weekend love my traeger and recommend the ironwood 885

title: Useless
text:

text:

title: Excellent Grill for Family of 4-7

title: Incredible grill! Wow

title: Awesome grill

title: Love this Traeger!
text: This Traeger is the best.  Lots of cool features, even many I never imagined.  Like the pellet drain system when you want to change flavors.  Or the multiple probes so we don’t have to guess  when pulling each person’s steak.

title: Everything I didn't know I needed
text: From extra large surface area, induction stove top, easy to clean grease and ash trap, storage area and shelves, insulated cover, easy to empty pellet bin, this smoker has so many things I didn't know I needed in a smoker, but I find that I use every single feature. title: Pro 34
text: I've had issues with the grill from day one.  It always runs about 25 degrees below the set temperature.  Also, I have never been able to get the grill above 410 degrees.  After 9 months of frustration, Trager finally sent me an new RTD.  It seemed to help maintain a more constant temperature but it didn't fix the problem of never getting up to temperature. I believe the digital temperature dial is bad. It doesn't seem to be reading the right temperature. I told the help line this but they seem reluctant to send me a new one. title: Perfect smoke

title: From Novice to Pit Boss!!
text: I have had my Traeger for about 6 months now and have nothing but praise to share! Not only was I a novice at grilling and smoking, no one would have ever accused me of being a technology wiz. Given that background, I was initially nervous that this Traeger would be too complicated for me. Thankfully, I have continually been shocked about the ease of operation of the Traeger. The WiFire connection and interface was quick to install and made operating the grill and preparing recipes as though an expert was right by your side. From igniting the grill, monitoring and adjusting the temperature, accurate probes to ensure correct internal meat temperature, recipes, timers, and shutdown, the entire cooking process couldn’t be easier. I have cooked a variety of proteins in a variety of ways ranging from reverse seating to long smoking, each with great success. The induction cooktop is an added bonus. I have noticed, however, that the cook time is longer on the Traeger induction burner than my kitchen induction stovetop. I attribute this to the cold outdoor temperatures during the winter months and am anxious to compare once the summer arrives. There is plenty of storage for accessories beneath the grill. The wooden cutting board that magnetically attaches to the pellet hopper did become “moldy” this winter and I ultimately took it off. Once again, I attribute that to the fact that I live in Washington State where it rains much of the winter. Others in a dryer climate may not experience this issue. Overall, I am thrilled with the new Traeger and look forward to many years of fun entertaining!

text:

The interior light is handy, but it would be nice to have one located on both sides of the grill and in the back. The temperature guide and ignition system are very easy to use.  Being able to monitor the grill temperature from my phone is also a great feature.  The side induction stovetop is convenient and provides an added cooking surface for sauces and sides. There is a lot of storage under the grill and the ash bucket is easily located and cleaned. I'm especially impressed with how easy it easy to control and monitor the grill through the Traeger app on my cell phone.  The app really works great.
The grill is very robust, and I have every confidence that it will last a long time.  The Ironwood 885 is not cheap, but I'm convinced it's worth the money.
The proof is in the results, and from the BBQ'd food we're getting from our Traeger (two meals now -- a smoked pork loin and a ribeye steaks), we're satisfied that this was money well spent.  
I can heartily recommend the Traeger Ironwood 885 grill.

title: Pound for Pound
text:
Long, but worth a read from someone who spent hard earned money for this smoker instead of receiving as a promotion*

To begin, I was a Traeger hater not because of social media but due to the fact that the Pro 22 I had 3 years ago wasn’t great. It was a basic entry pellet smoker and that was it; not a grill to sear or for use in the winter. From that point on, I went back to using other pellet grill brands and mostly charcoal grills such as a Kamado, a Bronco, and a MB 850. I had rid myself of the Traeger brand only committing to returning if they made something worth while with a better warranty. Low and behold, the year had arrived. 

I was a little skeptical at the beginning pre live stream “release” with even seeing a leaked box and price on reddit. I was a little offended by the price simply because I was a “hater” still and shrugged it off as stupid. The live stream happened and what everyone thought, I had believed as well: it was beyond beautiful but the tag was insane for a pellet grill. Two weeks went by & I kept going back to the new Traeger to look at it and understand that this is what I had personally wanted from Traeger: A larger warranty, no paint to peel from heat, and the ability to sear. The extras are a bonus such as better smoke flavor, and a new easy cleanup. 

So a week and a half before today’s (Apr 22) official launch that everyone could start buying, I purchased one which to me was a huge risk. Almost two weeks later I have to say it is living up to the hype. A little buggy from the get go (the automated seasoning pre programmed in the controller bugged out and stopped) but a massive improvement from previous models. I would say being well versed in grills or specifically pellet grills has helped with the new beta software, but she is a beaut. 

Smoke flavor is better than most if not all pellet grills on the market (still have not used super smoke-not needed much now) and I attribute this to the new delivery by the AI in the controller. From start up (literally from ignition) to shutdown you are receiving blue smoke constantly. It runs as smoothly as an offset in terms of constant delivery of wood flavor and smoke production (obviously taste is not the same considering scientifically pellets are just less moist for offset flavor). The induction works flawlessly and can produce excellent searing on your cast iron without overheating said cast iron and transferring cast iron flavor to your protein. 

I have to say I am impressed with the new Timberline XL and by the craftsmanship of the grill itself. Built to last is hard to relate to a reader but the paint is gone and replaced with an enamel type finish. The grill feels like its worth the money for once (sorry Traeger) and the 10 year warranty has at the very least quelled any fears for the future. In my opinion, this is Traeger's first “premium” grill. Not the timberline Gen 1. So as to whether it is worth it? Yes, absolutely. If you have the financial ability to do so, this grill does edge out most of the competition if not all of it. It’s a hard pill to swallow, but Traeger has finally earned my respect. I may not be a fan boy but this grill gives me the ability to defend the naysayers for once without being one myself any longer. Im more than happy with the product they rolled out and again, for once it looks like they have genuine care for a product of theirs in terms of build quality. Have a good one ya’ll. 

P.S. I still recommend purchasing a front shelf for extra space.

title: Damaged right out of the box. Not a good start
text: After months of time consuming research on what grill to go with. The ironwood 885 showed up today.  Couldn’t figure out how to open the lid after unboxing. Then i realized the the weld on the right hinge was broke and offset at an angle compared to the other. Which bound the lid up. Upon looking further the lid is offset to one side and the side of the barrel is a large bulge.  Then I realized the there is a dent in the front where the lid meets the barrel. It was clearly dropped at some point.  No idea how this works. I was looking forward to seeing if it blows smoke through the unsealed lid as a lot of reviewers have stated. Contemplated the timberline for this reason. Not sure what to do now..

title: Does not get to temp out of the box
text:
Having owned and cooked on several traeger grills in the past, I was excited to see traeger innovating with this new grill. I purchased this yesterday, got it all setup and went through the onboarding. Want to share my experience as “most” of the the other reviews online are from influencers. Having spent my own money on this I will give an honest review.

First, the good; this thing is a tank and was so well thought out on the build process. It looks absolutely beautiful and the tech in this grill is beyond anything out there with pellet grills.

Now the negative: After setting up I seasoned the grill with the automated onboarding setup. Everything appeared to be working but I noticed it was set to 500 halfway through the seasoning and would not get above 370. Once it hit 370 it actually started cooling down til it 70 degrees by the time it finished seasoning. No errors at all as a matter of fact it said seasoning complete.

I called support and after three hours of troubleshooting and testing it would appear the grill won’t get anywhere near correct temp. I can set the temp to 400 and it will sit at 170 and actually tell me it has reached the temp on the grill and on the app. (Keep in mind it took 25 minutes to get to 170). Traeger support was escalating to beta team and tier 4 support and said they would call me back and give me update.

They called me back and said they are thinking it might be firmware and they will probably get back to me sometime next week. The lady from support also said she just got off the phone with someone else that was having the EXACT SAME ISSUE! So I knew I need to write a review.

Here is my problem and I will change the review if this gets fixed but traeger released this grill to influencers nearly a month ago. I waited til yesterday when I could buy and after a month of beta testing with influencers you are still selling a nearly $4000 grill that basically is just a lawn ornament at this time and rather than sending someone immediately to fix, their answer was hopefully sometime next week as it might be a software issue and they have to figure it out.

I am extremely disappointed. I was super excited to get this grill. After finding out support had back to back calls on the first day around here we were able to buy, this is a major ball drop from traeger. Until they fix this, I will leave this review up. I will edit if they actually follow through with my experience when I can actually cook on it.

****Buyer beware if you are looking at picking this up this weekend****

title: Disappointed
text: Long but worth the read.  I was never a fan of Traeger, because I’ve always felt their grills didn’t get hot enough and didn’t smoke enough.  Well, after 4 weeks of vacillating, I took the plunge.  However, I refused to by this from anyone (including Traeger) that had a no return policy.   So I waited until Home Depot got it.  Well this new  xl gets crazy hot and smokes like a chimney.  The induction works great, and let’s just be honest, this grill on your deck makes you the talk of the town, because it looks incredible.  But at the end of the day, it all comes down to if the thing works.   First week, whole chicken, ribs, and chicken breast were absolutely amazing.  The smoke flavor was what you would expect and them some.  Then came week two.  Halfway through an 8 hour pork butt, I get a flame sensor error.  I call Traeger and they say I can finish the cook, but the grill won’t perform optimally.  Well, it stopped performing completely, and I had to fire up my trusty old Pitboss.  After trouble shooting and shining a light down into the fire pot toward the auger, the error code was gone.  They said it shouldn’t happen again.  Well, the next day, temperatures all 30% higher or lower than what I set it to, and then, the following day, another flame sensor error, right after I’ve prepped my wings to cook.  So those go back in the fridge and I spend time 30 more minutes on the phone with Traeger, with the solution being to simply fix it the way we did last time.  At that point, I was done,  so back to the store it went.  At the end of the day, this grill looks great, has great features, ideas, and concepts, but when I spend my own hard-earned money at the tune of 4K and more for the accessories, I need this grill to be flawless out the box, and not give me any issue for at least a couple years.  These were major issues, twice in the middle of a cook, and once right before a cook.   This grill should have been a home run,  but it just seems like there’s just too many moving parts adding up to too many potential problems.  And the fact that it was released with these and other issues I’m reading about is very disappointing.  All of this from a person who never writes reviews unless I’m completely blown away, or utterly disappointed.  In this case, it is definitely the latter.

title: Love the grill
text:
