We decided to review the grill…had also seen reviews it wouldn’t get to temp.
Set 500 and restarted it. Saw reviews about slow to get to temp, but it hit 500 in about 14 minutes. Not bad really.
We normally cook 225, so we lowered it. It kept a nice range.
Tried Super Smoke. Worked good too.
Probes paired without issue.
The app was a little flakey initially, saying the grill wasn’t online, when I knew it was because I could see it connected when I connected to my router.

So, maybe we’re lucky, I don’t know, but we absolutely love this grill.
Cooked ribeye, tritip, and salmon so far. Everything has come off tasting fantastic. We’re doing ribs right now and have a brisket set for the weekend.
The “only” negative is the pellet bin that comes with it. Somebody in quality control needs a talking to because it fails the Traeger name miserably. The bin cannot handle a full bag of pellets. It bows outward and loses its seal. That’s just basic there. Why would someone not test a bag of Traeger pellets in the bin? Like I said, complete quality control failure there. I hope Traeger does something quickly because the bins are like $30 and they’re complete crap. Pardon my French. We use ours to empty the hopper, then pour the pellets into a better container.

The grill though…we love it. Zero complaints.

title: It's a Smoker
text:
I’d love to give them a 5 – and certainly do for the food, but for the product, I have to drop to a 3. So I’ll make it a generous overall 4. I think they rolled it out before it was ready. Customers should never be the Quality Assurance department, and at this price point, there should be zero issues.
I have been using a lump charcoal smoker (Komodo style) for years, so know my way around smoking food. I was looking for a Natural Gas Grill for an outdoor kitchen I am building. I found the new Traeger Timberline and it said it was both a smoker and a grill, so I figured, one grill doing both products: Great! My lump charcoal smoker can also be used as a grill, but I liked the idea of "set it and forget it" temperature.
Well, yes you can grill on it, but the first time it took 1 hour and 45 minutes to get to 450-degree. I was on the phone with support for an hour of that - maybe more. I ended up eating a ham sandwich for dinner.
The second time it was quicker – 45 minutes. On a call with support, they told me the grill "learns" and will get faster each time. I hope so, because if it continues like this may end up with a gas grill anyway. They also said it takes loner because the heat is “indirect heat”. It is not like a gas or charcoal grill where the meat is right above the flames. Makes sense.
I will say this - the steaks were terrific.
I cooked a couple whole chickens at 350-degrees. I smoked them first at 225 for an hour, the brought it up to 350. Didn’t notice any issues with the temp. It got to 225 within 15 minutes and I wasn’t watching it go to 350 – I was watching the meat temperature. They were terrific too – very moist.
Smoked a 10-lb pork butt – very happy with that cook. Smoked for 22 hours with real issues.
I have no complaints about the food cooked in this – just the time to temp when grilling – and I hope that improves. It seems like it is.
Issues:
My second wireless probe never syncs to the grill.
The hopper is a poor design. It does hold an entire bag, but the hopper creates a hollow tunnel – like a whirlpool – where the pellets drop into the fire chamber. The pellet sensor is right over that, so I keep getting alerts that I am low on pellets, and I must move the pellets around in the hopper to make it happy again. Not cool on long cooks.
The grill seems to send a “Pre-Heat Finished” alert after 15 minutes – never when the grill is actually to the goal temperature. I’ve mentioned this to Traeger support while on my calls with them – they say they are looking into this.
Don’t buy this expecting to get rid of your gas grill. This isn’t that.
Doesn’t hold temp as well as expected. The walls are single wall construction, so it makes sense – I just wasn’t expecting it to vary as much as it did – about 10-degrees hotter at times, and a few degrees cooler. 
On the plus side:
The wireless technology is very good. My old lump charcoal smoker had a third party device that controlled the temperature and such, but it worked off Bluetooth. That was horrible. This thing lets me know what’s going on no matter where I am in the house. That’s a huge point in favor of this.
Does a great smoke flavor. I don’t notice the smoke rings that I saw on the lump charcoal, but definitely taste it.
The end result is a really tasty meal.
Traeger has exceptional customer support. I have never called for support and had the level of service these guys provide. They certainly set the bar for customer support.

title: Started off on the wrong foot, but it's a winner
text: When I saw the videos, I knew I had to have one.  I have an Ironwood 885 and wanted something larger. Went to my local Ace Hardware and purchased Timberline XL. They assembled it and delivered it. Followed the instructions to the letter, loaded up the pellets and started the seasoning cycle. The Smoker would not get past 190 degrees and went into the shutdown cycle. Tried again, same results. Contacted Trager support by text and that did not work well at all. Suddenly I see a message on the grill screen. It said, temperature sensor error and also said for me to take the drip pan out, the heat shield, and vacuum out the dust, pellets in the hot pot and try again. I'm thinking what dust?  It never heated up. I'm thinking I have an electrical issue with the sensor. Not happy at this point. After I calmed down, I decided to do what they asked before I called Ace to come get this thing.  As soon as I took it apart the problem was very obvious. There is a stainless steel sleave that fits inside the chute the pellets drop through to get to the hot pot. The sleave was not installed correctly, and the lip on the top was partially blocking the pellets coming from the auger and they were bypassing the chute. Only a few were actually getting into hot pot and igniting. I removed the sleeve, reinstalled it correctly. Put everything back together and tried again. Worked perfectly. Heated right up.  After the seasoning cycle was over, I put on two Tri-Tips and enjoyed a perfect cook. Used the two MEATER Probes that came with the Smoker, and all was fantastic.  Good luck Traeger trying to top this one. You just lost a customer as I don't think I will be in the market for another Smoker for many years to come.

title: Grill will not maintain Temperatures at 180°
text:
Traeger Technical Support Call Reference number: 01980833

TL:DR
Save your money for a grill that's not being Beta tested with paying customers. The kinks are NOT worked out with maintaining cook temperature.

I bought this grill over Memorial Day weekend 2022. I had high expectations for buying a premium smoker from a reputable company. The main function of the grill does not meet performance standards from my previous Ironwood 650 Traeger smoker. Per the representative, the acceptable tolerance for temperature variation is 25°F +/-.  This is trouble when trying to smoke ribs with the 3/2/1 recipe. I set the grill at 180° and would maintain temps ranging from 150°F- 165°F. This prolonged my cook from 6 hours to 9 hours based on meat temperature.. I'm order to keep the temperature at goal I would intermittently jack the temperature to above 180°F and dial down once goal was met. When calling customer service they were happy to tell me my average cook temperature was 175°F (thanks WiFire).  I stopped doing my workaround and the tech support was able to see the discrepancy in temperature.

Their recommendation was to run the grill's seasoning cycle... Again. I was frustrated to learn that there is an entire Beta team that was talked to fixed the issues with this grill.  These issues were known and Traeger still moved this grill to market.

Because of these cook issues the $100 worth of ribs (6 racks) were tough because of the extended cook times. I had to ensure the pork was safe to eat and not undercooked. The variants in cook temp caused doubt.

I asked to be compensated for the waste in Pellets and meat related to a sub- performing product. I called in 5/29 and was told that a manager will review the call and reach out to me. Review will stand until this situation is remedied. If no contact, then I'll be returning the grill to purchase a better performing grill.

Bluetooth temperature probe would disconnect from Bluetooth mid cook. Unable to set/reset temperature goals mid cook.

title: Great Features but:
text:
So this is my first Traeger and I went all in getting the XL. Beautiful grill, definitely for home us not competition. 
First I love the setting for the wired probes (has wireless more on that later) you can set the internal temps while maintaining a low smoke temp. It has a touch screen that is very user friendly with many features. The Timberline XL also has thick gauge stainless steel racks to last a long time. 
Now the problem: I had a party that I needed to cook a lot of food and the large cooking area was perfect. I wanted to use the wireless probes but could never get them to work nor had the time to call support. I had a whole top sirloin 2 pork butts and 1 whole packer and 1 flat to cook and all seemed to go well. Until I got to the stall. I wrapped the meats in foil and added the juice. At some point the juices worked their way out and down to the burner area. This coursed error code and this was late at night so no way to tear apart the grill and too hot as well as not knowing the grill. So the next day the sensor dried and fired up. After I was done and started the cleanup and discovered what I believe to be a flawed design. As you will see in the picture the base is designed to collect fluids on the left which worked well and collected fluid on the right which is the fire box. So you can’t cook any high fat meat nor use any fluid to break the stall on the right side dramatically killing 50% of your cooking surface. 
I do like the construction of the grill but my design would have a raised bevel to send juices to fat collector bucket not fire box. Traeger this needs to be fixed and parts sent out to customers. @ $3800 it’s the least you can do.

text:
Since day 1 this grill cannot hold temp above 350 degrees.  I've done all troubleshooting which includes:  3 different types of pellets including Traeger pellets, dry storage and removal of pellets after each cook, Cleaned RTD probe, Cleaned burn pot and grill after every 2 1hr cooks, Cleaned hopper dust, adjusted RTD probe away from wall, Adjusted chimney cap, and oiled fan. 

I've never been more disappointed in a purchase and should have never given this much effort into making it work, I should have just returned it.

title: So much better than my old smoker
text: Finally i can smoke a chunk of meat or a batch of salmon without constantly adjusting vents or fire or wood chips.  With this grill i can do a 20 hr pork butt AND get some sleep while i’m doing it!   Only complaint is that the door to empty the pellets is just about useless unless you’re OK with half of the pellets missing the bucket.  I have yet to find a way to get any kind of box or bucket in the right place so i can empty the hopper after a smoke. It works better with 2 people, one to hold the bucket and one to stir the pellets. I would have given 5 stars but knocked off a star for the hopper door and the bignprice tag.

title: Decent smoker, but not a grill
text: This is my first Traeger and I've been using it for about a month. It looks great and performs decently as a smoker, but don't expect to get rid of your regular grill. There's no way to get the timberline to grill or sear anything, and to try takes forever. I do love having it, and the food comes out great, but it doesn't do as much as advertised especially for the cost.

title: Worst Grill I've owned
text: Bought 8 months ago and have had nothing but problems with heating and usage since. Overpriced for mediocre at best Craftsmanship. I have used propane, charcoal, and other pellet grills and this is by far my least favorite. My favorite thing about this grill is waiting 3 hours to cook chicken breasts for my wife and kids at 9 at night. Full of superfluous gizmos and gadgets that do nothing but break and complicate your cooking. Would never own another Traeger and would never recommend to a friend. Extremely dissatisfied with this product.

title: Follow up to my from 20 days ago
text:
Have been very busy and unable to smoke any meat since my first review 20 days ago.
Ribeye steaks.  Set my cook temp to 450 degrees. Took about 15-20 minutes to reach that temp.  I was very happy as she climbed right up.  Yes, during the cook the temp moved back and forth from 460 degrees to 440 degrees.  12 minutes on each side and a perfect medium result which is what I wanted. Very happy with this new Smoker.

title: For the price, expectations not met one week in.
text: I’ve had the grill for a week and although the quality looks great with fit and finish, I’m having issues with an odd plastic/electric smell coming from the exterior grill at the bottom, when using temps above 400F. I had these same odors during seasoning and followed the directions exactly… just thought the smell would naturally go away. Support staff on the phone are nice and wanting to help, but they are always referring to the “team” to get an answer on moving forward. Time consuming for me and why not let me speak directly to the team?  As of today, a local Traeger repair rep will need to come out to investigate but that’s only after I have to call back again on Monday, to get the ball rolling.

title: Constantly broken
text: I bought this grill exactly one year ago.  I can count on my two hands how many successful cooks I’ve had.  Constant LER errors, hours of troubleshooting with traegers customer service (everyone I’ve dealt with in that department is great).  I keep it clean and always deep clean prior to smoking larger cuts.  Latest issues have been the auger feeding pellets continuously until I end up with fire in the auger tube.  CS worked with me to troubleshoot and sent me a new controller.  I installed it and tested by doing some burgers, all seemed well.  Picked up a brisket and had plans for a Memorial Day bbq, about 6 hours into the cook to dropped, ler error, I spent the rest of the day again troubleshooting with CS.  They decided it’s a bad auger motor now.  We ended up having to cancel our bbq and ruined a $80 brisket…I’ve always used traeger brand pellets, tried to do everything by the book and this thing has turned out to be a huge disappointment.  I’ll stick to my Weber kettle until traeger can do something to gain back my confidence.  I cannot leave this thing unattended so therefore can’t use it for its intended purpose of smoking.  CS was going to send a bag of pellets for my troubles, still haven’t seen those…

title: Terrible
text: We ordered the Timberline XL as our old Traeger broke (which we’ve had for 5 years) and we’ve never had an issue with Traeger. However, this grill has been nothing but a nightmare and frustration. We’re done with Traeger and would not recommend it to anymore after this experience now. We got it April, used it twice as soon as we got it, and then it just broke… They sent us 3 different motherboards. Which, we had to take apart the grill, then put it back together all 3 times, and all 3 didn’t work. They FINALLY sent us a brand new grill… After putting it all together it also doesn’t work. And every time it doesn’t work, we have to call, then told we need to speak to  a “Timberline CL specialist,” and then end up sitting on hold forever. You would think with spending this much money on a new grill all the kinks would be worked out before launching it. We’ve now gone almost 3 months with spending about $4,000, no grill, and nothing but a headache and frustration.

title: I love this grill
text: An incredible grill.  Easy to use.  Beautiful design.  Simple to assemble.  Wonderful

title: Might as well get a pit boss!!
text: I had a pro 22 before I moved overseas. Last Friday ordered the pro 34 thinking it would be a carbon copy of my pro 22 that I bought in 2018 only bigger.  Boy was I wrong. The stainless steel front handle is already starting to rust. And the heat defector where do I start? My old pro 22 had what was about a 1/4 inches defector and worked great no hot spots!! This pro 34 I just got is about 1/8 inches or less!! Beyond disappointed!! Would not recommend this product which is sad cause I was bragging about how great this product is!!

title: New Timberline
text: The grill is awesome!  It is so easy to use and is incredibly large, even this smaller one is huge.  Temperature is very accurate and the induction burner is awesome for reverse searing any steaks.  Assembly was very simple and initial setup went well.  Customer service is absolutely top notch as well.  Have called them twice and they could not be more helpful each time.

title: Wow what an experience
text: I love this smoker.   I've avoided getting one for several years because I thought it would be too much work.  I was wrong.  It was easy to assemble and even easier to use.   I smoked a brisket first thing and loved the flavor of the meat.  I'm getting ready to smoke a variety of meats this weekend to share with my family.

title: Overall - amazing and love it
text: After spending years mastering smoking over charcoal and block wood - I decided to invest in a Traeger. I love it. The only reason why I couldn't give it five stars (I wanted to) is because you can't use both wired probes without the grill defaulting to pizza oven mode. I know it's minor - but for the cost, frustrating.

title: Amazing!
text: This machine is expensive. But if you want the best they offer your gonna spend coin. Easy to use. Love the touch screen. Wish MEATER probes were integrated the same way they are in the MEATER app but maybe an update will change that. Love the cabinets under cook area. I will say it doesn’t seem like all the ash goes into keg clean out. But def less ash getting in and around food. I would recommend. Fingers crossed have not had any issues with mine.

title: Better in every way
text: I upgraded from the Timberline 1300 to the Timberline XL and I am loving it. It’s literally better in every way. So many small details have been upgraded along with the obvious things like the new design, induction stovetop, and new ash clean up. In my opinion it’s worth the money, an amazing smart grill/smoker. Just get it!

title: Very easy to use : follow the directions
text:
Timberline XL came boxed very well. Instructions via APP were extremely easy to follow. I’ve done three cooks so far and i can’t wait to do more. This grill is so easy to use and the included wireless thermometers make things even easier. You can’t mess food up. The grill cover is probably the most heavy duty cover I’ve seen. I am positive that this grill will last me for a very long time. If you’re unsure between the XL and regular, opt for the XL. You’ll find things to cook you didn’t think you would. 

A few people have stated that the grill gets above the set temp and i have experienced that but it goes down to what it’s preset to in a matter of minutes. 

One of the PAL rails was missing and through Traeger, they shipped me the piece with no hassle. So far I’m very pleased with the cooking experience and their customer support.

title: lid sensor error? what?
text: I purchased from Traeger my Timberline XL (yay).  Unboxing and assembly was a breeze.  It took about 2-3 hrs by my self.  They recommend 2 people, but I am a man.  Once I got it together, I was super excited to get rolling.  I did all the updates,(at least 90 mins) and the initial burn off (another hour).  I went to the grocery, got 2 whole chicken, 3 racks of pork spare ribs, and 7 full bones of beef ribs.  Seasoned up with my Meat Church Rubs, and on the grill it all went.  Disappointed that I didn't get more because there was more room on the grill, I was rolling.  That's when it happened.  Lid Sensor Error.  What was this?  I looked it up on the Traeger app,  It said that this was not a critical error, but that the grill would run at reduced performance.  Why, Traeger, Why?  Even if the lid were open, why reduce the performance?  Beyond that, I would imagine that the lid sensor error can only occur while in use.  Also, it can only be fixed by a shutdown cycle.  I have food on the grill!! Noooooo!!!!  Luckily I am a Mans Man and have now a total of 4 grills.  I left the XL on while I preheated my pro 780 and my Kamado.  I moved the food on to the other grills and after about an hour and a half with Traeger support and 2 full shutdown cycles, the code was cleared.  This was a real bad feeling when I just spent a total of 4500 on grill and accessories.  I understand not being able to test the flame sensor while the grill in on, but the lid sensor code should be able to be tested and cleared while in use.  This was my first cook on it.  I am cooking again this weekend and if I don't have any issues, I may revise this to higher that 2 stars.  I cant express how disappointing this was to have this occur on the first cook on the most expensive grill that I have ever purchased.  Traeger support was good and they hung in there with me through the online chat the whole time.  Had the support dropped the ball (which they did not), This review would have been titled "Returning my XL".  Thank you Traeger Support for your patients with me in this most trying of times.  To the guys making Traeger, Lid Sensor?  Why?  I dont need a lid sensor.  I have an app that tells me the when the temp is down.  My pro 780 does just fine without such non-sensor.  Please send an update allow this to be fixed while in operation or delete it completely.  In summary, I love my pro 780.  It is a marvel of modern engineering and a blessing to the world.  I really hope I feel this way about my XL in a few months.  But like my ex, this will take some time to get past.  I was broken hearted to say the least.  Especially when my wife gave the old " I told you so" about spending so much on a grill.  Whos kid needs college anyway.  Trades people are what we really need.

title: Next level smoking
text: The Timberline XL is next level when it comes to pellet grills. I went from an ironwood 885 to the timberline xl and it’s been a great addition. This thing rolls smoke like no other pellet grill I’ve seen. Consistent temperature at all ranges and so much room on the grill to cook anything you would like. I can’t wait to get more cooks on this thing. I’ve had it for a little over a week and have used it almost very day. I highly recommend adding the Timberline XL to your outdoor kitchen!

title: Love it
text: Have Only been able to use it a few times but I do love it

title: AMAZING IN SO CAL
text: THIS SMOKER HAS LIVED UP TO EVERYTHING PROMISED AND THEN SOME! THE APP IS AMAZING! I HAVE DONE RIBS, PORK BUTT, RIB EYES, AND PORK BELLY / CHUCK ROAST BURT ENDS AS OF TO DATE...ONLY 4 WEEKS IN!!! THIS IS A TOTAL OUTDOOR KITCHEN. FOLLOW THE TRAEGER VIDEOS AND YOU WILL GET AMAZING REULTS. I DID NOT USE THE SEASONINGS SOLD BUT DID USE TRAEGER PLELLETS. I WAITED FOR A LONG TIME TO PULL THE TRIGGER ON A TOP OF THE LINE SMOKER AND COULD NOT BE MORE SATISFIED!

title: The great smoker
text: My first and last smoker I will ever need and/or buy!! It’s simply that awesome!! Made my wife a believer too!

title: pro series 34 awesome smoker
text:
My wife and I brought out Smoker 10yrs ago We use it all year round. we had people here for holiday's and they love the taste of the food they keep coming back. Can't say enough of our smoker. But I as in me, did something wrong, and it caught on fire. I can't believe it all the years we kept up on it cleaned it cover it and kept it out of the weather. So, keep up on your smoker don't say I'll get to it the next time. Or you can do what I did and watch 10yrs of a great smoker go up in smoke. What a bummer. 
It takes less than a half hour to maintain your smoker Now to buy a new Traeger.

title: Extremely Disappointed
text: I want to start off by saying the Traeger is a great grill when it is working, I waited a long time to get my first Traeger last year a Pro 34 but after a few controller changes it would still cook 40-60 degrees hotter than the temp I set it at so after 9 months I took it back to Home Depot and upgraded to the Pro 780 and it worked great perfect temperature for less than 2 months then the controller and switch went out and after installing the new controller and switch that Traeger sent me it now runs 30 degrees hotter than where I set it, Traeger customer service has been great they are prompt in sending parts but I’m getting ready to take this back to Home Depot and get another Pro 780 because Traeger customer service informed me that they don’t have home service available where I live so I have to take it to a repair center, Traeger had a controller issue and they need to get it addressed, so I’m going to be on my third Traeger in less than a year all I want is a BBQ that lives up to the Traeger reputation that drew me to Traeger in the first place

title: Best Traeger ever.
text: This is my 4th Traeger and by far the best. It is so well made, high end parts for sure. Maintains the temperature perfectly.

title: Worth every penny
text: Wife bought me the Pro Series 34 and never looked back. It's so easy to use it's not even funny. It actually makes cooking enjoyable. First time I smoked some chicken breasts and turned out great. Next up was the brisket and for the first time smoking a brisket it turned out pretty darn good. You have to do your homework to make sure you cook these items. Steak, burgers and just did a pork tenderloin and it's one of those grills where I can't wait to cook again doing something new.

title: The Only Smoker
text: The best smoker I have ever used and the customer service and warenty help is outstanding. I personally wouldnt buy anything else. Good job Traeger

title: Does not maintain temp
text: I purchased the Pro780 1year ago and after 1 temperature probe and 3 controllers I still experience the same problem.  My grill cooks 30-40 degrees hotter than my setting.  This is known to only occur under 250 degrees, so “low and slow” is not possible.  A Traeger tech confirmed there is a known issue with the 575 and 780 but they do not have a fix.

title: Impressive grill, great results
text: This is an impressive grill that delivers great results.

title: It's just awesome
text: Moving from my first generation to this is like moving from a 72 'vette to a 2022 - they might have the same name, but they are not the same machine. Smoke is better, design is better, the overall functionality is better, and cleanup is so much easier. Brisket, pork butt, burgers, sausage, and more so far. While I am pleased with the performance, it does seem to take more time to get to temperature, but I will gladly take the improved smoke over time to temp.

title: We'll see
text: Difficult to connect to wifi. Arrived damaged from manufacturer. Took st least 1 hour to repair

title: Easy to use
text: I bought it just before Father’s Day and last night I cooked my first brisket which it should be done in about an hour. It stayed at temperature with some fluctuations and the wireless probe connected without a problem. This is an expensive smoker/grill and the real test will be this winter.

title: Easy to “use” but doesn’t hold temp
text: Been trying to smoke with this for several weeks. “Smoke” temp goes up to 275; large variation in temp so I can’t leave it for long. Right now trying to smoke a brisket and temp is at 280!  Very disappointing . Followed all the startup directions but just not very well engineered apparently. Been having problems since I bought it from Costco but finally decided to write because of the total frustration with it.

title: Grill is great, order system & support need work
text:
I ordered my first Traeger grill (Ironwood 885) directly from Traeger. It arrived about 7 days later but had some significant damage to the hopper. I have no way of knowing if it was damaged during packaging or during shipping. Without too much fuss Traeger agreed to send a replacement hopper which also included the auger assembly. The replacement hopper arrived 7 days later. There were no instructions with the replacement hopper so I had to contact support again. They emailed me instructions that were mostly accurate.

I had to contact support several more times to get a return shipping label to send the damaged hopper back.

This weekend I noticed that one of the seams on the grill cover was coming apart. Again I contacted Traeger support. Again without much fuss they promised to send a replacement cover.

Through all this my biggest complaint is they never once sent any shipment notifications. I did get a call from the freight company to arrange delivery of the grill but never received anything from Traeger on the initial grill order, replacement hopper and cover shipments. In fact their online order status on the initial order still said “Processing” even after I received the grill.

Having to contact support for hopper install instructions and return labels multiple times was aggravation I didn’t need. But they did stand behind their products.

When it was all said and done the grill is everything I hoped for.

title: Awesome Upgrade
text: I upgraded to the new Timberline XL from a 4 year old Traeger Pro. My Pro did great for grilling and would get good smoke using a tube smoker. However, I was excited to see if the new Timberline XL would do even better. Boy have I been blown away. The amount of smoke this thing puts off is incredible! Even without the Super Smoke setting turned on it pumps out great smoke. The Super Smoke really helps give you that nice smoke ring that is usually hard to achieve on a pellet grill. The price is steep, but it is worth every penny. Traeger does a fantastic job with great hardware and software. The Traeger app is remarkable. I believe the app puts it way ahead of its competition. Purchased this new Traeger from my local Ace and as always the service was wonderful!

title: Beyond disappointed with this purchase
text: We bought this grill about 3 months ago. It’s been nothing but issue after issue. Within the first month we had to replace the control panel. It just died witch resulted in our grill not being able to complete the shut down cycle. It just wouldn’t shut off. Cue first fire panic.  We managed that scare and Traeger sent a new panel. Now our pellet box is literally catching on fire. Where we not only lose all of our pellets, but  have to deal with this HUGE safety issue. Customer services acted like this was ordinary, and recommended we “sift” our pellets before loading them into the grill. This is not recommended or documented anywhere that I have looked, and honestly I’m having a hard time trusting this method. I am so disappointed not only with the grill but with customer service. Don’t use your grill if you think you’ll have to return it because it literally creates unsafe fires. They told us that because our grill was used it’s not their problem. Now we have a grill that I probably won’t even use with my fire extinguisher on stand by. It’s just not worth it.

title: No smoke ever
text: I bought an Ironwood 885 three months ago based on a friends recommendation.  His has smoke billowing out of it constantly but mine never has smoke.  I don't see smoke and I definitely don't taste any smoke flavor.  I've called customer service several times now and I always get the same answer.  They say there are no error codes on my burns and you are not supposed to see smoke.  It is called a smoker right? currently very disappointed with my $1500 purchase.  I have gone back to my $300 upright propane smoker until customer service figures out what is broken on mine.

title: Like a tank
text: Okay so I was given another brand of pellet grill you can find on amazon a while ago and decided to upgrade after major grease fire in previous grill. Bought the grill and without going into all the details the grill took a 5 ft high roll and tumble off a trailer (I know how dumb I am for that already, no more judgements please, lol). The shelf got bent and the lid got bent a little as well. That being said after making adjustments to said grill, everything is working amazing. We cooked around 50 hamburgers and 40 hot dogs this weekend, and the grill is just awesome. If I were to make one recommendation it would be to land the grill on all 4 wheels, and gently would be the key. But if you don't, this grill is built solid! Thank you Traeger!

title: Great Smoker
text: I have had my smoker for almost a year now. Its Incredible. Is it a stick burner? No its a pellet grill. The fact I can set it and forget it is Awesome! If I want some more smoke I can add a smoke tube, but so far I have not. Briskets, ribs, chicken pork and fish. My stick burner might as well be Retired. My Traeger works flawlessly. If it broke tomorrow I'd buy another in a second.

title: Best Grill Ever
text: I bought my Pro 22 4 to 5 yrs ago and LOVE it.  If it brought down anytime soon, I would another one immediately. Food is great

title: Traeger Ironwood 650 I’m a convert!!
text: I was not familiar with pellet grills, I’m officially a convert! So far I’ve been able to achieve what I thought was unthinkable! Delicious BBQ ribs, awesome perfectly cooked ribeyes, tenderloins, filet mignon, super juicy chicken, OMG, Traeger is the absolute total package, I feel confident and I’m sure of repeatability in every cook I do, super happy with this purchase and next recipes are queuing up soon!

title: Top of the line
text: Traeger has taken the new Timberline above and beyond regular smokers.  With its versatility and ease of use, it will become your new outdoor kitchen.  Smoking, grilling, searing, low and slow, it does it all!

title: Great bbq
text: It’s still early but used it 3x in a week and works as billed.

title: Not worth the money.
text:
I have had this grill for a little over a month a couple of cooks on it.  I purchased all accessories and the cover for it coming in at about 5200.  I have to say with the videos I watched and the way this grill was supposed to work I was expecting the perfect pellet grill.  I was terribly mistaken on this.  There are some great features to this grill but some that are terrible.   First the clean up on this grill is supposed to blow all ash into the keg located below the grill.   This does not happen at all it piles up and I still have to get a shop vac to suck up all the ash the grill creates. I switched from a Ironwood series gave it to a family member.  The clean up on the Ironwood was so much easier than this grill every time you cook on this grill it is a extensive cleaning process  to get cleaned up in order for your next cook when the Ironwood I feel was a lot easier and user friendly.  This grill has huge temp swing 50 degree temp swings and stays there for some time before coming back down.  Mine has about 3 spots where smoke constantly leaks around the seal on the lid so it always has smoke loss and temp loss.  Finally I keep my grill covered and under a carport the entire time I am not using it.  I take the cover off the other day and the two pieces of wood they put on the bottom for shelves have mold dots on them.   I am not impressed and wish I could get my money back and repurchase my  ironwood again.  I would not recommend anyone purchase this grill for that kind of money the quality is not there.  The food quality was just as good off the Ironwood I am getting off the new Timberline XL.

The goods Color screen, wireless connectivity.

title: My First Pellet Grill
text: The grill was heavier than I thought, but I was still able to assemble it by myself.  I have always heard good things about Traeger and I am not disappointed.  My first few cooks turned out some great grub.  I love the recipes on the app.

title: So disappointed
text: I purchased my 575 about 2 months ago.  I was excited to enjoy the control and ease of use it would give me.  So far it’s been a nightmare hundreds of dollars of ruined food.  I followed the recipes on the app and they take hours longer then it should.  The grill is super hot on the vent end and cool on the other.  I had the grill full and the butter sauce on one side  was burnt and the other side cold and solid.  A turkey we made was burnt on the bottom and raw on top.  The grill is maintained and clean.  There is no answer from Traeger on what the issue could be.  They said check and see if it’s level.  The fun and excitement are gone and I’m back to using my Broil King.  In the end all I do with it is roast at 400 cause I can’t cook any other way.  I don’t recommend Traeger at all.  Total let down

title: Great once you get it set up correctly (firmware)
text: I was SUPER disappointed at first for a few reasons. First, the wifi antenna is complete garbage. It also will ONLY work on 2.4ghz channel (not 5g), so I had to set up a guest 2.4ghz network on my router. The grill wouldn't work at all without the firmware update out of the box. Of course, there is no way to check for updates, so you just kind of have to sit there and wait. Took HOURS. Anyway, after a lot of cursing and yelling at the Traeger people, it finally connected with a strong enough signal to download the update which took like an hour. Once that was done, though, it's been flawless. I had a gen 1 Timberline previously, and this is better in every respect. It heats up quickly, and actually puts out a lot of smoke unlike the Gen 1.

title: Poor quality for the price
text: I have owned my Timberline 1300 for 45 days. I have loved it so far. I have used my grill a handful of times. I clean it after every cook to take care of. I cooked a whole brisket July 4th weekend. It turned out fantastic. 13 hours at 200 degrees, pulled it wrapped in butcher paper for another 5 hours at 250. I also had a pan of all day baked beans on the grill at the same time. When I pulled the brisket I turned the temperature up to 300 to finish the beans. Went in side, came back out later and pulled the beans. Best meal we ever had! Went to clean my grill the next day and the bottom left side of the exterior barrel was all bubbled up. I thought it was grease or condensation. Wiped it off and paint just came peeling off. I spent two hours on the phone with Traeger customer service and got the same pitch everyone else gets. Grease flare up, cosmetic damage, can't help you! This is wrong. How do you sell a grill for $2300.00 that cant with stand heat. I was told my cook data shows when my grill was set to 300 degrees it flared to 400 degrees. So what, the grill can be set to 500 degrees. I have owned high end grills my entire life and have never had paint peel. Now I have a 45 day old very expensive grill that has cosmetic damage I have to live with. Unacceptable, you need a better quality paint with a higher heat tolerance. My request for a new grill was denied. Don't think I can recommend Traeger!

title: Simply the best!
text: I purchased this the Timberline 1300 back in Sep 2020 to the surprise of my wife. To this day I don’t regret it at all, it was by far the best purchase I’ve made in years! Family and friends are always excited when we have them over to smoke some meats.

title: Excellent Grill
text: This is my 2nd Traeger. My first of which I still own and use was the Pro 575. However I wanted more food space and the super smoke option, so added the 850. Traeger simply makes the best grills period. For those who are new to smoker grills, get used to low and slow for the best tasting meats you've ever had.  I've perfected meats with a process that ends with an 18-20 hour smoke. Restaurants cannot compare to what I'm doing. In fact, the entire family doesn't like to eat out!  Trust me, buy what you can afford.  From Pro 575 on up, they are all great.  It is an investment, but well worth it. You will actually save money because you will eat out a lot less.  Finally their customer service is great. From the first time I called and I didn't understand the machine initially, the agents took their time with me and welcomed me into this community.  The agents also like to smoke themselves. And if there is any issue, you will be taken care of period.  There are various pellets you can use and most of them are great.  If you are new, start with the highest rated ones to get started.  You won't be disappointed.  Finally, check for a local authorized retailer near you.  If there is one close, they will have everything you need and more (at least my local store did).  When I found this well stocked Traeger retailer, it was like I was a young 5 year old boy walking into Toys R Us for the first time. Do you remember that feeling from years ago? They had grills, pellets, seasonings, accessories, and much more all around me.  Decades ago when I was 5, I didn't know a place was built only for toys that was all around me.  Now I have a new place that I didn't know ever existed.

title: To many problems with this new Timberline XL grill
text: I have had so much trouble with my Timberline XL with flame out sensor replaced twice, then the motherboard and nothing worked kept getting the flame out sensor error.  Then Traeger switch me out with a new Timberline XL grill only to get the same problem again.  Now waiting on a flame sensor for this  second new Timberline XL grill but nothing have been shipped out it's been going on two weeks and every time I call I have to wait countless hours just to get through.  I am so frustrated with this new Timberline XL grill and wanting them to just give my money back.

title: Product
text: Best Smoker/Grill in the market. Great for Pro’s or just the average grilled. No flare ups and the app showing temp and time is amazing.

title: Awesome Grill!
text: I got this grill for me and my wife. It is the perfect size for 2 people. We eat a mostly plant based diet and the veggies I've cooked on it thus far have been incredible. Solid product, works great- look sharp!

title: Nearly perfect
text:
This is my first pellet grill, and it’s nearly perfect. The double-walled sides and lid, with the full gasket, creates an excellent seal to stop thermal leak. The design and size are excellent, and I like having the recirculating smoke cake the chimney. The WiFi is awesome, and I’ve had no problems with any connection issues.

However, the meat temperature probe is way off, even after multiple calibration attempts. This was confirmed by my ThermoWorks Signals, thermapen, and a cheap store-branded thermometer. Further, the stainless steel shelf looks fantastic but functionally is worthless. It’s far too narrow to put food, trays, or really anything else on at all.

My last gripe is my biggest. Not because it’s a massive issue for grilling, but because it shows a lack of care and attention to detail:

The drip-tray liner doesn’t fit the drip tray. It’s not only the wrong size, it’s the wrong shape. I had ordered a pack that arrived before the grill arrived and had wondered if I bought the wrong ones. Nope! The grill came with one in the packaging that was exactly the same as I bought separately…completely the wrong size. This has been reported numerous times to Traeger and in reviews and they continue to sell and provide overpriced accessories that don’t fit the product. It shows a lack of care, and it’s a huge disappointment (and surprise) after spending thousands of dollars on an otherwise stellar pellet grill.

title: Worst unit I’ve ever owned.
text:
I’ve owned my Ironwood 885 for about a year and a half now. Had I known that a wood fired “grill” wouldn’t even sear a protein, I never would have bought it. I’ve placed the rack in its lowest position and set the temp to 500, the highest it would go and at most I get a grey looking meat. No Maillard reaction whatsoever on any protein I cook. I even went as far as to buy GrillGrates searing plates as they said they amplify the temperature upwards of 150 degrees hotter than the actual grill temperature. Even those don’t get any hotter than 530 degrees. The only useful thing is being able to set a temperature and walk away. It has no smoke flavor whatsoever. Traeger pellets have literally 0 flavor compared to other brands such as Lumberjack, which actually helps when I use them. In conjunction with a smoke tube though, because even at 180 degrees and super smoke on, there is no smoke flavor. The closest I’ve been able to get to a Smokey flavor was by putting pellets and wood chips in a smoke tube and cooking a brisket unwrapped for 13 hours, refilling the smoke tube up to 3x during that cook. And that was just a hint of smoky flavor. 

Their marketing team is genius as they make you think this is the greatest machine there is. And at one point I believe Traeger used to be respected. But with so many other options out there now, and then seeming like they just don’t care once they get your money, I’ve decided to sell my ironwood and go back to a stick burner offset. That’s smoky flavor. I even had to go as far as buying a Weber kettle 22” AFTER I bought my ironwood because the ironwood wouldn’t grill at all. It just bakes at a really hot temp. 

These “grills” are convection ovens. Not grills. And should not be marketed as a grill. It’s quite misleading.

text:
I've been an avid Traeger Grills fan since they started popping on the market. I have several Traegers, and decided to move from the Timberline 1300 to the Timberline XL. This thing is not ready for the market. First, when I got the grill - it came damaged with a cover. Apparently this was a common thing and they shut down replacing lids until they corrected multiple damaged covers. It took 4 months to receive a new grill cover.

Second, I am now stuck in a "Downloading Updates" loop to where I can't even use the grill. I let it run for 2 1/2 hours. Called support, they told me to let it run overnight. I called support again today, they told me to let it run for the rest of the day. Something's broke here. It's not a signal strength issue - my access point is literally right next to it.  Support has been extremely rough, not knowing the product or even how to escalate when I can't even use the grill now for several days. One person said it will attempt to download 5 times, then not again, another person said 4 times - then they said it could take up to several weeks to update? What? I can't use my smoker for several weeks? Are you kidding me? This is a complete failure here. 

The vacuum system is no better than the 1300. They claim it goes into the bucket, but most of the ash is still in the main floor of the smoker where you have to suck it out anyways just like you did on the 1300. Cleaning is the same, features just the same, and I would say my 1300 maintained more consistent temperatures and less fluctuating temperatures. The XL does heat up much faster which is a plus. 

I'm really disappointed in this grill. Once I get this downloading updates issue fixed, I plan on putting it up on the market to sell so that I can go to a different smoker. I have been a Traeger fan for years and always viewed them as the gold standard for pellet smokers, this has really soured my opinion on the grills and their build quality and for my move off of them completely.

title: Eh...
text:
My second review since launch, this one being an update to the experience. A long review but absolutely needed.

Traeger delivers with smoking in regards to the pellet grill market. The problem is that is all it does with minimal smoke improvement from the regular Timberline series. As far as searing goes I have to say it's atrocious without the induction. Yes, that is why the induction is there but tbh, I don't always want to use a pan to sear on. The gimmick is "wood fired" by pellet grills and a lot of the time, I want to sear on the grill itself specifically on the thick grates they updated to. What you get in return however, is a baked piece of meat. This is due to the grills incapability to revert back to a high searing temp quickly when the lid opens for even a couple seconds to flip something. Again, I understand the idea of the induction but it shouldn't have to be mandatory to grill. Some may agree when I say this, sometimes you just want to grill. By grill I mean you want to reverse sear and do it on the grill with that specific heat source.

 If I could return it I would. If traeger did a buy back, I would! The problem is manufacturers know that people will be displeased in the grilling community if their products don't live up to the hype so their return policy is "un opened un used" so in the end you're left wanting more, wishing more, and a grill going hardly used. In the realm of pellet grills, this is good for smoking. For a deeper flavor there are better brands for that, specifically OJ and Webers smokefire but this is better usual in terms of build quality. 

After allll that text what is the final recommendation? I would say you need to seriously consider what you want in a pellet grill, how often you think you'll want to sear on a pan and not the actual grill, and whether the very basic function of this grill outside of it's bells and whistles are what you'll truly be happy with. This isn't something I would recommend to the average joe. This Traeger comes off as a status symbol in my opinion and for a guy like me who could care less about that, I am now stuck with something I really do not care for. 

At it's basic core, it can smoke. Is it good enough at that to spend this kind of money? No. Will you be stuck with it if you end up disliking it after a long term period? Probably. Going on a month and no one has nibbled on my listing for it. It's a hard pill to swallow when listing a grill so beyond low for what you spent and still, no one wants to take that dive. That speaks volumes.

of any meat.
  But now Traeger has literally “Shook and Changed the Grilling and Smoking of Meats World” with the Totally Re-Designed, Very Sophisticated, Very Detailed and definitely The Most Advanced Pellet Smoker that any person can ever own with The Brand New Traeger Timberline XL!!!
  This Unit boasts an Amazing and Very Technologically Advanced New and Easy to Read Control Panel.
  All of the Entire Internal Components are now all
304 Grade Stainless Steel, which clean so much easier and also offers resistance to rusting and corrosion.

Apparently, that is a bridge too far without a lot of "testing" which isn't remotely convenient since the unit and my computer are not in close proximity to one another.  I went ahead and just ordered the thermocouple myself.  If this doesn't fix it, look for a video of us filling it up and Tannerite and "disposing" of it. title: Temperature Issues. Purchaser beware
text:
This grill was gifted for our wedding.. I was very excited to begin using it. The app is very  intuitive and easy to use, it was easy to assemble.  

What I've noticed, my first few cooks I've had significant trouble getting the meat up to to temp in the specified time. For example, 3,2,1 Ribs, after 6 hours were only at 140F (cooking at 220) Condering Traegers recipe tells you to hit 190 or 200F,  I resorted to finishing on the bbq so my guest could eat at a decent time. Embarrassing. 

  At first I thought it was the meat probe, so I checked with another probe and calibrated it, it was fine.   I read everything on the Traeger troubleshooting, used quality pellets, checked for air flow and gaps or anything blocking the heat etc.

What  I found is the cooking surface was significantly lower in temperature then what the digital controller was reading.  170F when the grill said 220. No wonder my food did not cook.

I got ahold of multiple people on the support line, which is handy as its basically text messaging, however there only check for the thermocouple is that is can read the ambient temperature fine and they send you an article about how third party thermometers shouldn't be used because "They cannot detect variance and hot and cold spots".   Well the cold spot is where the meat is cooked, so thats a problem lol.

 That's nonsense. The thermocouple on the grill is placed directly above the flame and fan so the heat  reading is off.   They told me its fine and basically to do better.   It was even suggested that the grill was sitting in the sun which compromised the accuracy lol, I live in southern Canada and its nearly winter. 

 If you research even a little bit online  you can see this is an ongoing issue with the grill Traeger obviously does not take seriously.  Not one that can't be overcome, but do not expect Traeger to take accountability. 

 I will be using my own oven thermometer  to monitor temperature moving forward and will update this review with my findings. I'm excited to use this grill again but cooking my own way, because even at low temperature the food has been great, so when cooked correctly I think it will be even better. 

If I had paid for this grill I would of returned it and purchased something less expensive that I knew I'd have to monitor myself.  At the very least, the meat probe is bang on, maybe I had too high of expectations for the digital controller.

title: Timberline 1300 is Fire, Literally
text:
The Timberline 1300 has ruined my Traeger experience.  I purchased a Pro 22 originally and absolutely loved it.  I cooked everything on that grill.  I hosted, neighborhood cookouts with 50 plus people, having to cook items ahead to manage with the smaller grill.  It was awesome, I was your typical Traeger fanatic always talking about my grill and probably have sold 10 to family and friends.  

Traeger released the new D2 models and I eventually went all in on the 1300.  It has been nothing but problems from day one with grease fires.  I keep the grill clean and have never had issues like this with the much cheaper Pro 22.  The issue is the Timberline series has a very poor grease management system.  They have little slope on this model's drip tray.  Then there is a 34" wide grease trough along the front of the grill to catch all the grease from that tray.  Whenever you cook above 300 with this model, you run the risk of a grease fire.  

It's really unfortunate because I never had any issues with the Pro 22.  I bought a Pro 575 more recently, and have had no issues with that one either.  

Sort these reviews and read all the fire complaints.  It's a major issue and essentially keeps me from using the grill for anything but smoking.  It's a real shame to have bought the top of the line model at the time and not be able to rely on it and use it.  I highly recommend if you want a Traeger, to get the Pro series or Ironwood series.  They are more reliable in my experience.

title: Easiest, best tasking Thanksgiving Turkey ever
text: I did my first turkey this year using the Traeger turkey brining and pellet kit ($27). Talk about a simple and easy preparation. We brined the turkey for almost 24 hours and then as the instructions on the packet said patted it dry, rubbed it down with a little oil and put the Traeger rub on it. We put it in a disposable aluminum pan and into the Traeger. The only other things we did was insert the temp problem and after a period of smoking, turned up the temp. This was on a 32 and below temperature day and still the bird was cooked to perfection. It has wonderful flavor and aroma. It beat out the oven roasted turkey by a mile. My wife who has taken great pride in doing the Martha Stewart turkey recipe in the oven next year even commented that the Traeger Turkey was no much less effort to prepare and was the winner on flavor. title: Problems.
text:
This traeger is absolutely a hunk of garbage. 2 days after purchase the auger broke. Treager unwilling to help, I returned it to Home Depot and got a new one. It has been a constant battle with this grill. It is horrible at maintaining ambient temperatures (even being covered with Treagers overpriced temperature retaining padded cover). The pellet bowl will constantly overfill and cause the traeger to shut off showing "LEF". If it doesn't shut off the massive amount of pellets will smolder and cause a nasty yellow smoke show ruining whatever food is inside, followed by a flash over causing the grill to be filled with giant flames and temperatures well over 500 degrees (yes, I only use Traeger brand pellets and yes I clean out the pellet bowl constantly, which in itself is a pain in the butt). This grill has ruined many special events for me and has destroyed a massive amount of fine meats that I have put a lot of effort and hard work into. I am deeply unsatisfied with this Traeger. Long ago I was passed down a Traeger grill that was my fathers for many years and it was a great product that continued to work for me for many years as well. These new products are not only overpriced, but are cheaply made and extremely disappointing. DO NOT buy this product or support this brand. 
I know this sounds like one of those typical annoying product rants that you read and dismiss but you will be better off passing on this product and going with a different brand. I am very ashamed with this Traeger and this brands overall cheaply made, overpriced products. Truly saddened that I will cannot recommend or stand behind this brand any longer.

text: The grill itself is beautiful, high quality, cool features, etc. I ordered it with every bell and whistle I could, and was in love with it, until I tried to set the grill up. After seasoning the grill I attempted to set up the Wi-Fire part of the grill, and have been less than successful. I have been on the phone on multiple occasions (4+ hours easy) with tech support, and there are so many hoops to jump through to "maybe" get the wireless to work, and still have not had any success. I guess I didn't read the fine print one how the Wi-Fire technology works. I have a new WIFI booster coming to try and remedy the situation, but I am skeptical. Bad thing about it is, the Bluetooth functions will not work either, so the side burner and wireless probes are useless at the moment. The whole reason I purchased the grill was for the amazing features that the Wi-Fire technology brings to the experience. I use my grill 4-5 times per week, year round, so to me it is a very important appliance. Right now it's just a $4K BBQ that does the same thing as my old standard Traeger, but with a cool digital screen. Long story short, make sure read exactly what is needed to make the Wi-Fire technology work before buying, and make sure it is dialed in before the unit arrives. This will save you a lot of headache and a lot of time with tech support.

Called service again spent 30+ mins again with diagnosing the problem ran a test and came back with numerous codes So they said it must be the motherboard replaced that on Friday Dec 16th DID NOT FIX PROBLEM Call service same day and spoke with a supervisor and reviewed all the problems and i asked for a refund or new grill said they needed to talk to their supervisor and would call me back in 24 hours. No call 
back!  Today spoke with friendly service rep that said they wanted to send me another part to see if that fixed it. It has been broken for going on 2 months I explained i bought this $3700 grill to use it, not to be a grill technician. I asked, could they asked if they could send someone out to fix it or could send me a new one i spent hours on phone with them and replacing parts.

Or i could load this 500 pound grill in my car and take it to a dealer in town to have it fixed.  DON’T BUY THIS GRILL unless you want to become a grill technician. They assured me that the total replacement of the hopper assemble will fix the problem, hopefully i will cook again in 2023. My mistake was I bought a $3700 grill direct from Traeger and cant return it like you can at other retailers if you get a lemon.

title: Timberline 850
text: Apologies ahead of time for the rant, but I feel it's a little overdue. Purchased the Timberline 850, and within a few smokes I noticed the powder-coating on the outside corner of the barrel beginning to bubble and fleck off. There were also the very beginning signs of surface rust, so I contacted customer support. I was told that their warranty doesn't cover paint/cosmetic damage, and only rust if there is an actual hole; and finally that I should just cover it up with a high-temp paint. First of all, for a +$2k smoker and such an acclaimed rugged outdoor appliance, I shouldn't have to touch up anything on it, especially within such a short period of time and after such ginger use. Secondly, it clearly states on your website that the warranty would be voided if I were to apply paint, as suggested by their CS team member. I clean all of my T's regularly, they have never had a flare up, and all of them, even my 850's short life, have been placed under a cover when not being used. Clearly the powder-coating wasn't applied correctly, thus the delaminating of it already And by the time a physical hole actually does rust through the barrel, the warranty will have lapsed. I'm disappointed that they don't just address the problem and make it right. I've owned many Traegers myself, and purchased a few for family and friends solely because of their CS team and willingness to help out a fellow BBQ enthusiast. Quality has gone down and their customer service isn't what it use to be. There was a time when Traeger would have bent over backwards for their customers, but I believe that time has come and gone.

title: 3 MONTHS STILL BROKEN
text:
My last review was 15 days ago when they sent me a new fix, the hopper assemble. After receiving it it looked easy on the video to install but the video does not show all the steps to remove and replace the hopper and there has been always one screw the strips so you have to remove that problem as well. One and a half hours later i got it close to installed but did not work I had one wire that i didnt know where it went and the video does not show you how or where they go. Called service TWO HOUR WAIT. So I decided to call the next day and spoke to a tech and  we finally got it installed but it was the same problem that I originally called in on in Oct.
She said she would escalate it to and should have an answer on Tues because Monday was a holiday. Call on Tuesday spoke with another tech he had me get it online and update the software and run a diagnosis and still had same two faults as in OCT.
He said he would have an answer in 24 hours and to call and they would have a resolution to the problem. I received  an email with a new case number and instructions to call in 24 hours and the would have a resolution to my problem. I thought Great i finally going to get a fix to the problem after 3 months. Called today 24 hours later as email stated gave my case number new tech said, No it could take 3 to 5 business days or when ever the engineers get to look at it, so it could take longer.
I asked if i should call every day to find out if they got a resolution and he said no they would call me. The last Tech told me after another promise to call within 24hours that Traeger does not promise to call anyone back. Now i am confused I have a $3700 broken grill that i got to use 2 months and have no idea when or if it will ever work. 
I have spent hours working on this grill and have replace every part that they have sent.
I would not buy this grill unless you have the skill set, the time and the tools and want to make your life miserable.

title: Grill awesome / App TERRIBLE
text:
Bought grill in May 2022. After a couple uses, igniter went out. Took about a month to get replacement. So, rough start. The grill, when it runs, is outstanding. The wifire part though and the app, not so much.
Have had intermittent grill connection with the app from the start. Updates fail.
So, after a number of calls I was informed that the grill has to connect to the app in order to update. Since I was having issues with the app...no update.
I was told that the grill only uses 2.4ghz wifi. This, I knew, was a part of the documentation. What they don't tell you is if the app is on a device which can also use 5ghz...like, oh...every device in 2022, now 2023, you will have the problems I was having. Despite being on the same network, the grill and app have issues.
The solution I was given was that I had to split my wifi bands into separate SSID's (wifi network names). One for 2.4, one for 5. When I wanted to use the grill, I need to switch the device with the app to the 2.4 network name. Devices which can use either band, I now have to force them to use one or the other.
So, I don't know which to blame here, the app or the grill only capable of 2.4ghz, but, my phone ran about $1200. It can use 5 or 2.4. My $4000+, modern...less than year old...grill/app can't. To me, the app should be able to handle to device being on the same network as the grill, regardless of what band either is connected to, but my expertise here is 0, so...
In any case...grill cooks fantastically. The wifire/app though could use some work.

text:
I have had the timberline 850 for two years now and sad to say it just ok as I love to cook, especially grilling and had much higher hopes for this grill.  My single biggest issue is keeping it clean. Anyone that knows anything about grilling knows it all starts with a clean grill and this grill is ridulously tedious to clean. I have had several weber grills over the years and the primary concern there is keeping the grates clean but with the Timberline 850 its way more than keeping grates clean. I spend two hours cleaning it for every 6-8 hours of cooking.  

I keep my grill in the garage when its not being used to keep it protected and have learned how critical it is to make sure its perfectly level because even if its just off slightly in a way the reduces the juice and grease flow the clean up is even more difficult and time consuming.  The drip pan covers need to be installed perfectly or they too will restrict the grease flow and create additional clean up issues.  It just seems to be a poor design for a high end grill.  I have a shop vac dedicated to cleaning this grill and even with that to clean it right you have to remove quite a few screws to remove interior covers to adequately g clean the nooks and crannies. The best feature is that is great a holding a temperature and contolling it with the wi-fire app is very convenient.  Even so, I find myself using my old charcoal weber grill more and more simply becuase I dont want have to deal with the clean up of theTraeger.  I pretty much only use the Traeger when I am cooking a large amount of food for 6 people or more to justify the cleaning of the grill.  I guess I am not the only one that feels this way as the clean up issue seems to have been addressed with the newer models.  If you are consideing buying a Treager, I strongly suggest you look at the new model with the EZ clean pot to avoid a situation like mine where you spend alot of money on a grill that is only used selectivelydue due to the hassle of cleaning it.

text:
I've had a mixed experience with my Traeger over the last year and a half. When using it at low to mid temperatures, I've been able to achieve a nice bark and smoke flavor on my pork and brisket, and the ease of use is a plus.

However, I wouldn't say that the Traeger is a jack-of-all-trades grill like it's advertised. While it can reach temperatures up to 500 degrees, it requires meticulous cleaning beforehand to avoid grease fire, which can melt the powder coat off of the grill. Additionally, the amount of pellets and time it takes to reach high temperatures is not very efficient.

In my experience, the Traeger is best used as a smoker rather than an all-purpose grill. All of the people I know who own a Traeger also own another grill, including myself. 

One issue that I've encountered is the quality of the powder coat. After experiencing a grease fire because I missed one spot in the grill when cleaning, the coat bubbled and flaked off, which is unacceptable. I'm not the only one in my Traeger circle who has experienced this issue, so it's something to keep in mind.

title: General pros and cons
text:
I've had my 780 grill for about 10 months and use it a minimum of 3 times per week. Previously I had a Traeger Bronson for 5 years and wanted to upgrade. I have to admit the 780 is bigger than I need, and at that time I should have purchased the 575, but here are my findings after cooking on the 780 over 120 times so far. 
The right side and across the front area of the grill are every large areas of cold spots. The biscuit test proved to me that these areas are not prime for maintaining high enough temps. I don't know if the firepot is just not adequate enough to heat the entire area or what might be the answer. Maybe relocating the firepot closer to the right side so that heat spreads across the grill better, to the chimney on the left?
I don't use the wifi option so I can't comment on that. It's just not an important upgrade for me. 
I believe it's because of the large interior space, but none-the-less I've had to increase the temp by anywhere from 25-50 degrees and/or increase the cook times in order to get the same results for many of my routine recipes.
The firepot itself collects ash more readily than my previous Traeger, instead of blowing  the ash into the cavity below the drip tray, causing me to vacuum it out far more often, and causing the grill to heat more slowly, when the firepot is so full of ash, after only short a short time prior to the previous vacuuming.
Because of the large amount of air cavity, it uses far more pellets than my previous Traeger in order to keep that much area at, or close to, the set temp, even though I have an insulation blanket on it year round.
Where the grease flows down into the trough is a much bigger pain in the neck to clean out than the Gen 1 Traegers.
Although it's not a big deal, I'm not a fan of the on/off switch, then setting the temp, plus then pushing the ignite button. The gen 1 Traeger's are easier and faster to start than the Gen 2, in my opinion.
All that said, I'm going to purchase a Pro 22 in the Spring when they run their first seasonal sale, that way the savings will pay for a front tray and part of the cost of a cover. I'll also purchase an insulation blanket because I grill a lot during the cold months and it's a great addition for Winter cooking. 
I'm going back to a smaller grill, because it suits my needs better, and I'm going back to a Gen 1 grill because I like to controller system better for me personally.
Some of my findings are strictly personal, and may be no problem for others, but it never hurts for a company like Traeger to get constructive feedback, no matter what it might be.
I would not buy another brand of pellet grill because I truly feel Traeger is a quality company that produces some great quality items. I hope my comments help some of you who are on the fence and are also helpful to Traeger.

There are two issues that make this grill not as good as our old one that got damaged.  That old grill made absolutely the best grilled chicken on the planet.  When the fat from the chicken dripped off on to the foil lined drip pan, it would bathe the chicken in wet steam when it it hit the drip pan which keeps the chicken moist and crisps up the skin perfectly.  As this occurred, more smoke would develop and exhaust out of the chimney.  The issue with this one is that the overwhelmingly vast majority of smoke always comes out of the outlet where the grease trap is.  The chimney has virtually no smoke when it operates which is completely different from our older one!  I called Traeger to discuss this issue and was actually told it wasn’t a problem!  The chicken on the new one is nowhere near as good as the old one and imparts little to no smoke flavor.  In addition, the drip bucket doesn’t catch near the same amount of grease as our old one.  In fact, I have only had to empty the drip bucket once since I’ve had it and I have no idea why it is so radically different than the old one.  The second problem is that the old drip pan showed virtually no signs of rusting over a lot of years of use while the new one shows tons of rust every time I change the foil out that protects the pan.    Both were always kept in my garage and only rolled out when I wanted to use it.  Overall, the new one doesn’t perform nearly as well as the old one.  And with all Traegers, they never get hot enough to produce a decent sear even though the temperature read out says it gets to 500. title: Blowing Smoke But No Bite.
text:
I bought this same grill from a local authorized dealer, which was a great experience. However, I have to say that my immediate experience with the grill itself was very disappointing. I set out to season the grill as recommended and later cook four racks of ribs according to Traeger’s 3-2-1 recipe. Everything looked great according to the perceived temps. I’ve cooked this same recipe on a competitors wood fired grill and it was on the money, so I naturally thought with the Traeger Timberline XL the cook would be even better. Unfortunately, it was one of the worst cooks I’ve ever done. I knew something was up when I grabbed the ribs from the 2-hour shift and didn’t witness ANY bone separation, but I continued the cook as directed. To note, I did make the mistake of just following the recipe, but I can assure you the grill was the main problem. I finally got the ribs on the plate and when we bit in…the ribs were raw closest to the bone. Apparently, the perceived ambient temp of the grill was off by some 50 degrees. So, instead of it sitting at 225 for two hours regarding one part of the cook, it actually sat at 175. I only realized this afterwards when I tested another cook of Pork Ribs with a third party remote thermometer. This thermometer broke the case wide open when it read the ambient temp at minus 50 degrees of the registered temperature reading on the grill. 

Working with customer service proved to be a waste of time since they determined that the grill needed a new thermocouple, which required me to disassemble the grill that was a week old. Not exactly ideal. I would later speak to the regional sales manager, and he assured me the local authorized dealer would send one of their associates to install the thermocouple. Well, at a $4,000+ price tag considering tax, you would think the company had enough to pay a certified tech to stop out and perform additional tests. To say the least, the thermocouple DID NOT fix the grill temperature issue. Moreover, the sales manager assured me that he would not allow Traeger’s customer support to start “parting” me to death. His words were, and I quote, “I will only throw one part at a grill, and if it doesn’t work we’ll replace it all together.” So much for that, the first thing he did was ignore my subsequent calls to identify the part didn’t work, and would later claim that any third party thermometer should not be trusted; however, Traeger has actually bought that very same technology from the third party thermometer company and have incorporated their tech into the new Traeger wireless thermometer system. Go figure! Either way, I eventually elected to return the grill to the local authorized dealer, which was a chore in and of itself. Regardless, I’m happier without the headache wondering if my next cook would be ruined. Essentially, I had to cook some chicken in the old pellet grill because the Traeger just didn’t get to temp as expected. 

Be weary of this product line. Period.

title: 1 Year In and Still Loving the Timberline 850
text:
The Timberline 850 makes grilling and cooking easy to do with consistently delicious results.  It smokes meat much better than some critics would have you believe (I say that comparing it to my Big Green Egg).  Temperatures are easy to adjust and once you set a temperature, the Traeger does a great job of maintaining the desired temperature even in 20-degree weather.  

Technology:  The WiFi feature works flawlessly.  If you have a solid home WiFi network (no interference or distance issues) then you will absolutely love the ability to control your cook from your phone.  

Durability:  I regularly clean the outside of my grill and keep an eye on the fire pot although it hasn't ever needed cleaning (despite the reminder message I'm greeted with every time I start the Traeger--it's a standard message you'll see when the system is booting up).  The very back metal plate of the grill showed signs of paint peeling, but that's my fault--I had the unit too close to my brick wall at 500 degrees for many hours.  A light sanding and some flat black paint took care of that little mistake.  

Customer Service:  I had an initial warranty claim (interior metal shield was warped upon delivery) and Traeger got me a replacement in two days without issue.  The rep was very knowledgable and did a good job handling the issue.  

While I do like my Egg for some types of cooking, I use my Timberline 850 more often.  There is no doubt that if I had to choose one grill it would be a Traeger.  I easily get 85-90% of the quality results of the Egg 100% of the time--and all I have to do is push a button.  

This is my second Traeger in 10 years and I highly recommend it.
